<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:topology-1}
    We say that $(A, \phi) \in H^1_\mathrm{loc} (\mathbb R^2)$ is an \textit{finite-energy configuration} on $\mathbb R^2$ if
		\[
			 \| A \|_{L^4 \, \cap \, \dot H^1}+ \| {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^2} + \| 1 - |\phi|^2 \|_{L^2} + \| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^\infty \, \cap \, H^1} 
                < \infty.
		\]
	We denote the space of finite-energy configurations by $\mathfrak E$, and the sub-class thereof satisfying the Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}) by $\mathfrak E_{\mathrm{df}}$. Furthermore, we endow $\mathfrak E$ with the topology induced by the following maps:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=({\roman*})]
			\item the covariant gradient,
				\begin{align*}
					\mathfrak E 
						&\longrightarrow L^2 (\mathbb R^2)\\
					(A, \phi) 
						&\longmapsto {\bf D} \phi,
				\end{align*}

			\item the Gauss tension field, 
				\begin{align*}
					\mathfrak E 
						&\longrightarrow (H^1 \cap L^\infty) (\mathbb R^2)\\
					(A, \phi) 
						&\longmapsto \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,,
				\end{align*}

			\item the inclusion map\footnote{By Lemma \ref{lem:gerard}, the scalar field resides in the ambient space $(L^2 + L^\infty) (\mathbb R^2)$ whenever $\tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2) \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$. },
				\begin{align*}
					\mathfrak E 
						&\longrightarrow (L^4 \cap \dot H^1)(\mathbb R^2) \times (L^2 + L^\infty) (\mathbb R^2)\\
					(A, \phi) 
						&\longmapsto (A, \phi).
				\end{align*}
		\end{enumerate}
	We also introduce the (slightly weaker\footnote{Continuity of the map 
		\begin{align*}
			\mathfrak E 
				&\to L^\infty (\mathbb R^2),\\
			(A, \phi)
				&\mapsto \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,,
		\end{align*}
	where $L^\infty (\mathbb R^2)$ is endowed with the norm topology, plays almost no role in any of our analysis. We mainly want (for convenience of statements) a topology which is characterised by its convergent sequences, and the Gauss tension fields of these sequences to be uniformly bounded. An alternative approach would be to work with a closed ball in $L^\infty (\mathbb R^2)$ with the weak-$*$ topology. 
	}) metric on the space of finite-energy configurations,
		\begin{align*}
			\operatorname*{dist}_\mathfrak E \bigl( (A, \phi), (A', \phi') \bigr) 
				&:= \bigl\| \delta {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2} + \bigl\| \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{H^1} + \bigl\| \delta A \bigr\|_{L^4 \, \cap\, \dot H^1} + \bigl\| \delta \phi \bigr\|_{L^2 + L^\infty},
		\end{align*}
	using the notation\footnote{Refer to Section \ref{subsec:prelim-notation} for further explication.} $\delta \mathsf U := \mathsf U - \mathsf U'$ for differences. Given an interval $I \subseteq \mathbb R$, we write $C_t (I \to \mathfrak E)$ for the space of continuous maps $I \to \mathfrak E$ endowed with the standard topology.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:gwp}
	The Cauchy problem for the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}) in DeTurck gauge (\ref{eq:DeTurck}) with initial data in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}) is globally well-posed in the space of finite-energy configurations in the following sense: 
		\begin{itemize}
			\item \textup{(Existence).} For each finite-energy configuration $(A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}) \in \mathfrak E_\mathrm{df}$, there exists $(A, \phi) \in C_t ([0, \infty) \to \mathfrak E)$ solving (\ref{eq:CSS-DT-intro}) with initial data $(A, \phi)_{|t = 0} = (A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}})$. 
			
			\item \textup{(Unconditional uniqueness).} If $(A', \phi') \in C_t ([0, \infty) \to \mathfrak E)$ is another solution to (\ref{eq:CSS-DT-intro}) with initial data $(A, \phi)_{|t = 0} = (A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}})$, then $(A, \phi) = (A', \phi')$.

			
			\item \textup{(Continuous dependence).} For each $T > 0$, the data-to-solution map,
				\begin{align*}
				\mathfrak E_{\mathrm{df}}
					&\longrightarrow C_t ([0, T] \to \mathfrak E),\\
				(A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}) 
					&\longmapsto (A, \phi),
				\end{align*}
			is continuous. 
		\end{itemize}
	Furthermore, these solutions satisfy the following conservation laws:
		\begin{itemize}
			\item \textup{(Conservation of abelian Higgs energy).} For all $t \geq 0$, 
				\begin{align*}
					\mathcal E_{\textup{AH}} [A(t), \phi(t)] 
						&= \mathcal E_{\textup{AH}} [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}].
				\end{align*}


			\item \textup{(Conservation of topological degree).} For all $t \geq 0$, 
				\begin{align*}
					\deg [A(t), \phi(t)] 
						&= \deg [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}]. 
				\end{align*}
		\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
One could probably also establish well-posedness in the affine Sobolev space $(\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}) + H^1 (\mathbb R^2)$ for each finite-energy configuration $(\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \in \mathfrak E^{\mathrm{df}}$. On the one hand, this gives more information about the flow $t \mapsto (A, \phi)(t)$, since the $H^1$-metric is stronger than the $\mathfrak E$-metric (see Proposition \ref{prop:magnetic-lip-1}), and suggests that the flow ``preserves'' the spatial asymptotics of the scalar field $\phi$. On the other hand, the $H^1$-metric is ill-suited for comparing configurations with different spatial asymptotics (see Appendix \ref{subapp:example} for examples), so in this sense the uniqueness and continuous dependence statement in Theorem \ref{thm:gwp} can be regarded as stronger.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
We can also pose the Cauchy problem for the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation in other gauges. In fact, we conduct the bulk of our analysis in an auxiliary gauge with better regularity properties, albeit being more difficult to state. One can then read-off the regularity in another gauge by estimating the gauge transformation. For comparison, the transformations to the DeTurck, temporal, and Coulomb gauges are given respectively by
		\begin{align*}
			\chi^{\text{D}}
				&:= - (\partial_t - \Delta)^{-1} (A_t - \partial^j A_j),\\
			\chi^{\text{T}}
				&:= - \partial_t^{-1} A_t, \\
			\chi^{\text{C}}
				&:= - \Delta^{-1} \partial^j A_j. 
		\end{align*}
	The temporal gauge, which may seem natural due to revealing the Hamiltonian structure of the equations, is obtained by solving an ODE, so we can expect it to be a full derivative rougher compared to the Coulomb and DeTurck gauges, where one can use elliptic and parabolic smoothing. At the other end of the spectrum, the Coulomb gauge, while favourable at high-frequencies, is difficult to estimate for low-frequencies, since the electromagnetic field is not well-localised. As a concrete example, the electric potential under Coulomb gauge takes the form
		\[
			\Delta A_t
				= \partial^j \Bigl( \varepsilon_{jk} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi) + \partial_j F_{12} \Bigr).
		\]
	Heuristically, $|\phi| \to 1$ at spatial infinity, so the most one can read-off here is $A_t \in \dot H^1 (\mathbb R^2) \subseteq \mathrm{BMO} (\mathbb R^2)$. The lack of control over low-frequencies unfortunately causes several technical issues.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:stability}
    Let $N \in \mathbb N_0$ be a non-negative integer, and suppose that $(A, \phi) \in \mathfrak E$ is a finite-energy configuration with topological degree $N$ such that
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:small-self-dual}
            \int_{\mathbb R^2} |({\bf D}_1 + i {\bf D}_2) \phi|^2 + |\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,|^2 \, dx 
                \ll_N 1. 
        \end{equation}
    Then there exists a self-dual vortex $(\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \in \mathcal M^N$ such that 
        \[
            \bigl\| (A, \phi) - (\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \bigr\|_{H^1 \times L^2}^2 
                \lesssim_{N} \int_{\mathbb R^2} |({\bf D}_1 + i {\bf D}_2) \phi|^2 + |\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,|^2 \, dx. 
        \]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:orbital}
    Let $N \in \mathbb N_0$ be a non-negative integer, $|1 - \lambda| \ll_N 1$, and suppose that $(A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}) \in \mathfrak E_\mathrm{df}$ is a finite-energy configuration in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}) with topological degree $N$ satisfying (\ref{eq:small-self-dual}). If $(A, \phi) \in C_t ([0, \infty) \to \mathfrak E)$ solves the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation in DeTurck gauge (\ref{eq:CSS-DT-intro}) with initial data $(A, \phi)_{|t = 0} = (A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}})$, then
        \[
            \sup_{t \geq 0} \int_{\mathbb R^2} |({\bf D}_1 + i {\bf D}_2) \phi|^2 + |\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,|^2 \, dx 
                \ll_N 1,
        \]
    and consequently, for each $t \geq 0$ there exists a self-dual vortex $(\mathring A(t), \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}(t)) \in \mathcal M^N$ such that 
        \[
            \bigl\| (A(t), \phi(t)) - (\mathring A(t), \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}(t)) \bigr\|_{H^1 \times L^2}^2 
                \lesssim_{N}  \int_{\mathbb R^2} |({\bf D}_1 + i {\bf D}_2) \phi|^2 + |\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,|^2 \, dx.
        \]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
Inspecting the statement of \cite[Corollary 1.2]{Zhao2026} more closely, one can upgrade the distance between the solution and self-dual vortex from $H^1 \times L^2$ to $H^1 \times H^1$, at the cost of the implicit constant depending on $\| A \|_{L^4}$. In DeTurck gauge (\ref{eq:DeTurck}), this unfortunately means the constant can grow in $t$, though one can remove the growth by working in a different gauge. We plan on returning to this point in future work.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
The analogous results for negative topological degrees follow by reflection.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
In the low-energy regime and near self-dual coupling, i.e. $|1 - \lambda| \ll 1$, the dynamics of vortices with topological degree $N$ under a geometric flow arising from the abelian Higgs energy $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{AH}} [A, \phi]$ can be modeled for long time by a corresponding flow arising from an effective energy on the moduli space of self-dual vortices $\mathcal M^N$.
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
Let $\chi$ be a sufficiently regular real-scalar field, and set 
        \begin{align*}
            \widetilde \Phi 
                &:= e^{i \chi} \Phi,\\
            \widetilde A 
                &:= A + d \chi.
        \end{align*}
    Then we have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item gauge-invariance of the magnetic field, 
            \begin{equation}
                F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}} = \widetilde F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}},
            \end{equation}

        \item gauge-covariance of the covariant derivative 
            \begin{equation}
                {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi 
                    = e^{-i \chi} \widetilde {\bf D}_{\bf a} \widetilde \Phi. 
            \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Expanding the right-hand side and using the famous identity $\partial_{\bf a} \partial_{\bf b} = \partial_{\bf b} \partial_{\bf a}$ yields
            \begin{align*}
                \widetilde F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}} 
                    &= \partial_{\bf a} \widetilde A_{\bf b} - \partial_{\bf b} \widetilde A_{\bf a} \\
                    &= \partial_{\bf a} (A_{\bf b} + \partial_{\bf b} \chi) - \partial_{\bf b} (A_{\bf a} + \partial_{\bf a} \chi) \\
                    &= (\partial_{\bf a} A_{\bf b} - \partial_{\bf b} A_{\bf a}) + (\partial_{\bf a} \partial_{\bf b} \chi - \partial_{\bf b} \partial_{\bf a} \chi) = F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}}. 
            \end{align*}

        \item Expanding the right-hand side, it follows from the product rule that
            \begin{align*}
                \widetilde {\bf D}_{\bf a} \widetilde \Phi 
                    &= (\partial_{\bf a} - i \widetilde A_{\bf a}) (e^{i \chi} \Phi) \\
                    &= e^{i \chi} \bigl((\partial_{\bf a} - i \widetilde A_{\bf a}) \Phi + i \partial_{\bf a} \chi \, \Phi\bigr) \\
                    &= e^{i \chi} \bigl( (\partial_{\bf a} - i A_{\bf a}) \Phi + i(\partial_{\bf a} \chi - \partial_{\bf a} \chi) \Phi\bigr)= e^{i \chi} {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi.
            \end{align*}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \textup{(Covariant derivative commutator identity).} 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:commute}
                [{\bf D}_{\bf a}, {\bf D}_{\bf b}] 
                    = - i F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}}. 
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Bianchi identity).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:bianchi}
                \partial_{\bf a} F_{{\bf b} {\bf c}} 
                    = \partial_{\bf b} F_{{\bf a} {\bf c}} - \partial_{{\bf c}} F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}}. 
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Covariant Laplacian commutator identity).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:laplace-commute}
                [{\bf D}_{\bf a}, {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j]
                    = -2i F\indices{_{\bf a}^j} {\bf D}_j - i \partial^j F_{{\bf a} j} .
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Covariant product rule).}
            \begin{align}
            \partial_{\bf a} (\overline \Phi \Psi) 
                &= \overline{{\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi} \Psi + \overline \Phi {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Psi. \label{eq:product}
            \end{align}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Applying the product rule and commuting mixed partial derivatives, 
            \begin{align*}
                [{\bf D}_{\bf a}, {\bf D}_{\bf b}] \Phi
                    &= (\partial_{\bf a} - i A_{\bf a}) (\partial_{\bf b} - i A_{\bf b})\Phi - (\partial_{\bf b} - i A_{\bf b})(\partial_{\bf a} - i A_{\bf a})\Phi \\
                    &= - i \left(\partial_{\bf a} (A_{\bf b} \Phi)  + A_{\bf a} \partial_{\bf b} \Phi - \partial_{\bf b}(A_{\bf a} \Phi) - A_{\bf b} \partial_{\bf a} \Phi \right) \\
                    &= - i (\partial_{\bf a} A_{\bf b} - \partial_{\bf b} A_{\bf a}) \Phi = - i F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}} \Phi.
            \end{align*}
        \item Commuting mixed partial derivatives, 
            \begin{align*}
            \partial_{\bf a} F_{{\bf b} {\bf c}} 
                &= \partial_{\bf a} (\partial_{\bf b} A_{\bf c} - \partial_{\bf c} A_{\bf b}) + (\partial_{\bf c} \partial_{\bf b} A_{\bf a} - \partial_{\bf b} \partial_{\bf c} A_{\bf a})\\
                &= \partial_{\bf b} (\partial_{\bf a} A_{\bf c} - \partial_{\bf c} A_{\bf a}) - \partial_{\bf c} (\partial_{\bf a} A_{\bf b} - \partial_{\bf b} A_{\bf a}) = \partial_{\bf b} F_{{\bf a} {\bf c}} - \partial_{{\bf c}} F_{{\bf a} {\bf b}}.
        \end{align*}

        \item Commuting covariant derivatives a l\'a (\ref{eq:commute}) gives 
        \begin{align*}
            {\bf D}_{\bf a} {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \Phi
                &= {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_{\bf a} {\bf D}_j \Phi - i F\indices{_{\bf a}^j} {\bf D}_j \Phi \\
                &= {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi - i {\bf D}^j \big( F\indices{_{\bf a}_j} \Phi\big)- i F\indices{_{\bf a}^j} {\bf D}_j \Phi \\
                &= {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi - 2i F\indices{_{\bf a}^j} {\bf D}_j \Phi - i \partial^j F_{{\bf a} j} \Phi,
        \end{align*}
    which, upon rearranging terms, proves the identity. 

        \item By the usual product rule and remarking $\overline{(-i A_{\bf a} \Phi)} \Psi + \overline \Phi (-i A_{\bf a} \Psi) = 0$, we compute
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_{\bf a} (\overline \Phi \Psi) 
                &= \overline{\partial_{\bf a} \Phi} \Psi + \overline \Phi \partial_{\bf a} \Psi \\
                &=  \overline{\partial_{\bf a} \Phi} \Psi + \overline \Phi \partial_{\bf a} \Psi + \left( \overline{(-i A_{\bf a} \Phi)} \Psi + \overline \Phi (-i A_{\bf a} \Psi) \right) = \overline{{\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi} \Psi + \overline \Phi {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Psi,
        \end{align*}
    which gives the result. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
The following inequalities holds in distribution:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \textup{(Diamagnetic inequality).}
            \begin{equation}
                |\partial_{\bf a} |\Phi|| \leq |{\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi|.\label{eq:diamagnetic} 
            \end{equation}
        
        \item \textup{(Parabolic Bochner inequality).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:bochner-heat}
            (\partial_s - \Delta) |\Phi| \leq |({\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j) \Phi|.
            \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Writing $|\Phi|^2 = \overline \Phi \Phi$, we compute using the product rule (\ref{eq:product}) and Cauchy-Schwarz 
        \begin{align*}
            |\partial_{\bf a} |\Phi||
                &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{\overline \Phi \Phi}} |\operatorname{Re}(\overline \Phi {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi)|\\
                &\leq |{\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi|, 
        \end{align*}
    as desired.

        \item Writing $|\Phi|^2 = \overline\Phi \Phi$, we compute using the product rule (\ref{eq:product}),
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_s |\Phi|
                &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{\overline \Phi \Phi}} \operatorname{Re}(\overline \Phi {\bf D}_s \Phi), \\
            \Delta |\Phi|
                &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{\overline \Phi \Phi}} \left(\operatorname{Re}(\overline \Phi {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \Phi) + \overline{{\bf D}^j \Phi} {\bf D}_j \Phi - \frac{\operatorname{Re}(\overline \Phi {\bf D}^j \Phi) \operatorname{Re}(\overline \Phi {\bf D}_j \Phi)}{\overline \Phi \Phi} \right).
        \end{align*}
        The main observation is that last two terms in the identity for $\Delta |\Phi|$ combined are non-negative by Cauchy-Schwarz. Upon another application of Cauchy-Schwarz, we conclude that 
            \begin{align*}
                (\partial_s - \Delta) |\Phi| 
                    &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{\overline \Phi \Phi}} \left( \operatorname{Re}\left(\overline \Phi ({\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j) \Phi\right) \right) - \frac{1}{\sqrt{\overline\Phi \Phi}} \left( \overline{{\bf D}^j \Phi} {\bf D}_j \Phi - \frac{\operatorname{Re}(\overline \Phi {\bf D}^j \Phi) \operatorname{Re}(\overline \Phi {\bf D}_j \Phi)}{\overline \Phi \Phi}  \right)\\
                    &\leq \frac{1}{\sqrt{\overline \Phi \Phi}} \left( \operatorname{Re}\left(\overline \Phi ({\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j) \Phi\right) \right) \\
                    &\leq |({\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j) \Phi|,
            \end{align*}
        as desired. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
Strictly speaking, the proofs above are merely formal arguments, ignoring technical issues when $\Phi(x) = 0$. One can easily make the arguments rigorous by a standard regularisation, replacing $|\Phi|$ with $\sqrt{|\Phi|^2 + \varepsilon}$, testing against non-negative test functions, and taking $\varepsilon \to 0$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
We have the following pointwise inequality
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:maximum-principle}
            |\Phi(x,s)| 
                \leq e^{s \Delta} |\Phi_{|s = 0} (x)| + (\partial_s - \Delta)^{-1} \big|\big({\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \big) \Phi (x)\big| .
        \end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
This follows from the parabolic Bochner inequality (\ref{eq:bochner-heat}), Duhamel's formula, and the fact that the heat kernel is non-negative.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item covariant derivative commutator,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:commute-diff}
                [\delta, {\bf D}_{\bf a}]
                    = \delta A_{\bf a},
            \end{equation}
        
        \item covariant Laplacian commutator,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:commute-diff-laplace}
                [\delta, {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell] 
                    = \delta A \cdot {\bf D} + \delta \partial^\ell A_\ell + \delta A \cdot A,
            \end{equation}

        \item composition of difference with magnetic derivative,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:diff-magn}
                \delta {\bf D} = \nabla \delta + \delta A + A \delta.
            \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Fix an arbitrary complex scalar field $\Phi$. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item We compute 
            \begin{align*}
                \delta {\bf D}_{\bf a} \Phi 
                    &= (\partial_{\bf a} - i A_{\bf a}) \Phi - (\partial_{\bf a} - i A_{\bf a}') \Phi' \\
                    &= (\partial_{\bf a} - i A_{\bf a}) (\Phi - \Phi') - i (A_{\bf a} - A_{\bf a}') \Phi' = {\bf D}_{\bf a} \delta \Phi - i \delta A_{\bf a} \Phi' .
            \end{align*}
            Rearranging gives the result. 

        \item We compute 
            \begin{align*}
                \delta {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \Phi
                    &= (\partial^\ell - i A^\ell) (\partial_\ell - i A_\ell) \Phi -(\partial^\ell - i {A'}^\ell) (\partial_\ell - i A_\ell') \Phi'\\
                    &= (\partial^\ell - i A^\ell) (\partial_\ell - i A_\ell) (\Phi - \Phi') + \bigl(  (\partial^\ell - i A^\ell) (\partial_\ell - i A_\ell) - (\partial^\ell - i {A'}^\ell) (\partial_\ell - i A_\ell') \bigr) \Phi'\\
                    &= {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \, \delta \Phi - 2i (A_\ell - A_\ell') (\partial^\ell - i{A'}^\ell) \Phi'  - i \partial^\ell (A_\ell - A_\ell') \Phi' - (A^\ell A_\ell - {A'}^\ell A_\ell') \Phi' \\
                    &= {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \, \delta \Phi - 2i \delta A_\ell {{\bf D}'}^\ell \Phi' - 2 \delta A_\ell  {A'}^\ell \Phi' - i \delta \partial^\ell A_\ell \Phi'  - (A^\ell + {A'}^\ell) \delta A_\ell \Phi' .
            \end{align*}
        Rearranging gives the result.
        
        \item We compute 
            \begin{align*}
                \delta {\bf D} \Phi 
                    &= (\nabla - i A) \Phi - (\nabla - i A') \Phi'\\
                    &= \nabla (\Phi - \Phi') - i A (\Phi - \Phi') - i (A - A') \Phi' ,
            \end{align*}
        which is of the desired form. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
Symmetrisation the notation and calculations would yield cleaner schematic formulas. For example, the difference of covariant Laplacians can be written as 
        \[
            {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \Phi - {{\bf D}'}^\ell {{\bf D}'}_\ell \Phi'
                = -\tfrac12 i (A - A')^\ell ({\bf D} + {\bf D}')_\ell (\Phi + \Phi') - \tfrac12 i \partial^\ell (A - A')_\ell (\Phi + \Phi').
        \]
    The cost is that we need to symmetrise the definition of ${\bf D}$ in the schematic notation. Taking the ``wrong'' magnetic derivative can be quite dangerous (see Appendix \ref{app:example}), so we avoid the symmetrised notation.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \textup{(Magnetic Bethuel-Smets inequality\footnote{The reader should compare with \cite[Lemma A.1]{BethuelSmets2007}.}).} Let $\Phi \in X^2_A (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
            \begin{equation}
                 \|{\bf D} \Phi \|_{L^4_x} 
                    \lesssim \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x}^{\frac12} \ \|{\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12}.\label{eq:GN4} 
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Magnetic Agmon inequality).} Let $\Phi \in H^2_A (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
            \begin{equation}
            \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x} 
                \lesssim \| \Phi \|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \ \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12}. \label{eq:GNinfty}
            \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Integrating-by-parts and applying Cauchy-Schwartz yields 
            \begin{align*}
                \|{\bf D} \Phi\|_{L^4_x}^4
                    &\approx \int_{\mathbb R^2} {\bf D} \Phi \cdot {\bf D} \Phi \cdot {\bf D} \Phi \cdot {\bf D} \Phi \, dx \\
                    &\approx \int_{\mathbb R^2} \Phi \cdot {\bf D} \Phi \cdot {\bf D} \Phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi \, dx \lesssim \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x} \ \|{\bf D} \Phi\|_{L^4_x}^2 \ \|{\bf D}^{(2)}\Phi \|_{L^2_x}.
            \end{align*}
        Rearranging gives the result. 

    
        \item Consider the following instance of the usual Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality,
            \[
                \| w \|_{L^\infty_x} \lesssim \|w\|_{L^1_x}^{\frac13} \|\nabla^{(2)} w\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac23}.
            \]
        Applying this to the gauge-invariant quantity $|\Phi|^2$ yields
        \begin{align*}
            \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x}^2 
                &\lesssim \| |\Phi|^2 \|_{L^1_x}^{\frac13} \ \| \nabla^{(2)} |\Phi|^2 \|_{L^2_x}^{\frac23} \\
                &\lesssim \|\Phi\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac23} \left( \| {\bf D} \Phi\|_{L^4_x}^2 + \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x} \|{\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\|_{L^2_x} \right)^{\frac23} \\
                &\lesssim \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x}^{\frac23} \ \|\Phi\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac23} \ \| {\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac23},
        \end{align*}
    using the covariant product rule (\ref{eq:product}) in the second line, and the magnetic interpolation inequality (\ref{eq:GN4}) in the third line. Rearranging and taking appropriate roots gives the result. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Let $n \in \mathbb N_0$ be a non-negative integer, $j = 0, 1, \dots, n$, and suppose $\Phi \in H^{n}_A (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:L2-interpolation}
                \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    \leq \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{1 - \frac{j}{n}} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n}},
            \end{equation}
        \item Let $n \in \mathbb N$ be a positive integer, $j = 1, \dots, n$, and suppose ${\bf D}\Phi \in H^{n - 1}_A (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:GN-interpolation}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/j}_x} 
                \lesssim \| {\bf D} \Phi \|_{L^2_x}^{1 - \frac{j}{n}}  \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n}} .
        \end{equation}      
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The first non-trivial case is $n = 2$ and $j = 1$, which follows immediately from integration-by-parts and Cauchy-Schwartz. 
            \begin{align*}
                \int_{\mathbb R^2} {\bf D}\Phi \cdot {\bf D} \Phi \, dx 
                    &= - \int_{\mathbb R^2} \Phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi \, dx \\
                    &\leq \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}.
            \end{align*}
        With this strategy in mind, we proceed inductively on $n$, assuming the result holds for $n$, and aim to prove the result for $n + 1$. 
        
        We divide into two cases; first, when $j = n$, we have
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    &\leq \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n - 1)} \Phi\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \,\bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 1)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12}\\
                    &\leq \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12 (1 - \frac{n - 1}{n})} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)}  \Phi\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12 \frac{n - 1}{n}} \,\bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 1)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12},
            \end{align*}
        using the base case in the first line, and the induction hypotheses in the second line. Rearranging yields the desired result. 

        Second, when $j = 1, \dots, n - 1$, we have
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                    &\leq \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{1 - \frac{j}{n}} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n}} \\
                    &\leq \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{1 - \frac{j}{n}} \, \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{(1 - \frac{n}{n + 1})\frac{j}{n}} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 1)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{n}{n + 1}\frac{j}{n}},
            \end{align*}
        directly applying the inductive hypothesis and the $j = n$ case. Simplifying the exponents, we see that this is precisely the desired result. 

        \item Consider the following instance of the usual Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality,
            \[
                \| w \|_{L^{2n/j}_x} 
                \lesssim \| w \|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n}} \, \| \nabla w \|_{L^2_x}^{1 - \frac{j}{n}}.
            \]
        Applying this to the gauge-invariant quantity $|{\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi|$, using the diamagnetic inequality (\ref{eq:diamagnetic}), and then interpolating the $L^2$-magnetic Sobolev norms via (\ref{eq:L2-interpolation}), we obtain
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/j}_x} 
                &\lesssim  \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n}} \, \bigl\| \nabla |{\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi|\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{1 - \frac{j}{n}} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(j)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n}} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(j+1)} \Phi\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{1 - \frac{j}{n}}\\
                &\lesssim \| {\bf D} \Phi \|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n} (1 - \frac{j - 1}{n - 1}) + (1 - \frac{j}{n})(1 - \frac{j}{n - 1})} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac{j}{n} \frac{j - 1}{n - 1} + (1 - \frac{j}{n}) \frac{j}{n - 1}}. 
        \end{align*}
        Simplifying the exponents, we see that this is precisely the desired result.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
Let $\Phi \in X^2_A (\mathbb R^2)$, and suppose that $1 - |\Phi|^2 \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$, then
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:inefficientLinfty}
            \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x} 
                \lesssim 1 + \big\|1 - |\Phi|^2\big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac13} \ \big\|{\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac13}.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Consider the usual Agmon inequality,
        \[
            \| w\|_{L^\infty_x} 
                \lesssim \bigl\|w\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \bigl\|\nabla^{(2)} w\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12}.
        \]
    Applying this to the gauge-invariant quantity $1 - |\Phi|^2$ yields
        \begin{align*}
            \big\| 1 - |\Phi|^2 \big\|_{L^\infty_x} 
                &\lesssim \big\|1 - |\Phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \ \big\| \nabla^{(2)} |\Phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \\
                &\lesssim \big\|1 - |\Phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \left( \|{\bf D} \Phi\|_{L^4_x}^2 + \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x}  \ \big\|{\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\big\|_{L^2_x} \right)^{\frac12}\\
                &\lesssim  \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x}^{\frac12} \ \big\|1 - |\Phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \ \big\| {\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12},
        \end{align*}
   using the covariant product rule (\ref{eq:product}) in the second line, and the magnetic interpolation inequality (\ref{eq:GN4}) in the third line. Inserting this into a trivial triangle inequality bound gives
        \[
            \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x}^2 
                \lesssim 1 + \|\Phi\|_{L^\infty_x}^{\frac12} \ \big\|1 - |\Phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \ \big\| {\bf D}^{(2)} \Phi\big\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12}.
        \]
   Interpolating, we can absorb the $L^\infty_x$-term to the left-hand side, completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:gerard}
    Let $\Phi \in L^1_\mathrm{loc} (\mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb C)$ be a scalar field such that the charge density satisfies $1 - |\Phi|^2 \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$. Then there exist $f \in L^\infty (\mathbb R^2)$ and $g \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$ such that 
        \[
            \Phi 
                = f + g,
        \]
    with
        \begin{align}
            \| f \|_{L^\infty_x} 
                &\leq 3,\label{eq:Linfty-part}\\
            \| g \|_{L^2_x} 
                &\leq \big\| 1 - |\Phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x} \label{eq:L2-part}.
        \end{align}
    Furthermore, if ${\bf D} \Phi \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$ for some magnetic potential $A$, then $f \in X^1_A (\mathbb R^2)$ and $g \in H^1_A (\mathbb R^2)$ with
        \begin{align}
            \| f \|_{X^1_A}
                &\lesssim 1 + \| {\bf D} \Phi \|_{L^2_x}, \label{eq:Lp-part1}\\
            \| g \|_{H^1_A} 
                &\lesssim \| 1 - |\Phi|^2 \|_{L^2_x} + \| {\bf D} \Phi \|_{L^2_x}.\label{eq:Lp-part2}
        \end{align}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
We cut-off $\Phi$ according to its amplitude, fixing a smooth cut-off $\chi \in C^\infty_c (\mathbb C \to [0, 1])$ such that 
        \[
            \chi(\Phi) 
                := 
                \begin{cases}
                    1,  
                        &\text{if $|\Phi| \leq 2$,}\\
                    0, 
                        &\text{if $|\Phi| > 3$},
                \end{cases}
        \]
    and setting 
        \[
            f:= \chi(\Phi) \Phi, \qquad g := (1 - \chi(\Phi)) \Phi.
        \]
    Then (\ref{eq:Linfty-part}) is clear from construction, and (\ref{eq:L2-part}) follows from the pointwise bound $|g| \leq |1 - |\Phi|^2|$, which holds since $|\Phi| \geq 2$ on the support of $g$. For higher regularity, we compute
        \begin{align*}
            {\bf D} f 
                &= \chi(\Phi) {\bf D} \Phi + \chi'(\Phi) \nabla |\Phi| \Phi, \\
            {\bf D} g 
                &= (1 - \chi(\Phi)) {\bf D} \Phi - \chi' (\Phi) \nabla |\Phi| \Phi,
        \end{align*}
    then (\ref{eq:Lp-part1})-(\ref{eq:Lp-part2}) follows from the diamagnetic inequality (\ref{eq:diamagnetic}) and $|\Phi| \leq 3$ on the support of $\chi'(\Phi)$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:interpolate}
    Let $\mathcal K > 0$ and $2 \leq p, q \leq \infty$ and $n_0 \in \mathbb N_0$. If $\mathsf U : \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s] \to \mathbb C$ is a sufficiently regular complex-scalar field satisfying
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:L2-base}
            \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
                \lesssim_n \mathcal K,
        \end{equation}
    for each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$, then
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:interpolate}
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^p_x}
                \lesssim_n \mathcal K.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By the interpolation inequality (\ref{eq:GNinfty}) when $\mathsf D = {\bf D}$, or its non-magnetic counter-part when $\mathsf D = \nabla$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12} (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^\infty_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\|  (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}^\frac12 \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n + 2)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}^\frac12 \\
                &\lesssim_n \mathcal K,
        \end{align*}
    using (\ref{eq:L2-base}) in the second line. This yields (\ref{eq:interpolate}) for $p = \infty$. For the non-endpoint cases, we interpolate
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^p_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}^{\frac2p} \bigl\| s^{\frac12} (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^q_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^\infty_x}^{1 - \frac2p} \\
                &\lesssim_n \mathcal K,
        \end{align*}
    using (\ref{eq:L2-base}) and the $p = \infty$ case in the second line.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:bilinear}
    For sufficiently regular scalar fields $\mathsf U, \mathsf V : \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s] \to \mathbb C$, we have  
        \begin{equation}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 \cdot \mathsf U \cdot \mathsf V \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                \lesssim \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \mathsf V \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) \mathsf V \bigr\|_{L^2_x},
        \end{equation}
    where $\mathsf D \in \{ \nabla, {\bf D}\}$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
We compute 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 \cdot \mathsf U \cdot \mathsf V \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) (\mathsf U \cdot \mathsf V) \bigr\|_{L^1_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \mathsf V \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) \mathsf V \bigr\|_{L^2_x},
        \end{align*}
    using the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality (along with the diamagnetic inequality (\ref{eq:diamagnetic}) in the case $\mathsf D = {\bf D}$) in the first line, and the product rule in the second line and Cauchy-Schwarz in the second line.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
Let $A$ be a connection $1$-form on $\mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the Yang-Mills heat flow (\ref{eq:YMH}). 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \textup{(Linear heat equation).} The magnetic field satisfies 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:F12-heat}
            (\partial_s - \Delta) F_{12} 
                = 0.
        \end{equation}
        In particular, the divergence-free part of the magnetic potential satisfies 
        \begin{equation}
            (\partial_s - \Delta) \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A_x
                = 0.\label{eq:A-heat}
        \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Linear transport equation).} $F_{sj}$ is divergence-free,
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:Fsj-transport}
            \partial^j F_{sj} 
                = 0.
        \end{equation}
        In particular, if $A$ is in caloric gauge (\ref{eq:caloric-prelim}), then the curl-free part of the magnetic potential satisfies,  
            \begin{equation}
                 \partial_s \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A_x 
                    = 0. \label{eq:A-transport}
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Commutator identity).} The covariant derivative satisfies the identity
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:parabolic-commute}
                \bigl[ {\bf D}_j, {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \bigr]
                    = 2i F\indices{_j^\ell} {\bf D}_\ell.
            \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item By the Bianchi identity (\ref{eq:bianchi}) and the Yang-Mills heat flow equation (\ref{eq:YMH}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_s F_{12} 
                &= \partial_1 F_{s2} - \partial_2 F_{s 1} \\
                &= \partial^\ell ( \partial_1 F_{\ell 2}- \partial_2 F_{\ell 1}) \\
                &= \Delta F_{12}.
        \end{align*}

        \item By the Yang-Mills heat flow (\ref{eq:YMH}) and anti-symmetry, 
        \begin{align*}
            \partial^j F_{sj} 
                &= \partial^j \partial^\ell F_{\ell j} \\
                &= \varepsilon_{\ell j} \partial^j \partial^\ell F_{12} \\
                &= 0.
        \end{align*}
        Imposing the caloric gauge, this identity reduces to the transport equation for the divergence,
            \[
                \partial_s \partial^j A_j = 0.
            \]


        \item Using the commutator identities (\ref{eq:commute}), (\ref{eq:laplace-commute}), and the Yang-Mills heat flow (\ref{eq:YMH}),
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl[ {\bf D}_j, {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \bigr]
                    &= i \bigl( F_{sj} + 2 F\indices{_j^\ell} {\bf D}_\ell + \partial^\ell F_{j \ell}  \bigr) \\
                    &= 2i F\indices{_j^\ell} {\bf D}_\ell.
            \end{align*}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Parabolic smoothing).} For $1 \leq q \leq p \leq \infty$ and non-negative integers $n \in \mathbb N_0$, 
            \begin{equation} \label{eq:standard-heat}
                \big\| s^{\frac1q - \frac1p} (s^\frac12\nabla)^{(n)} e^{s \Delta} u_0 \big\|_{L^p_x} 
                    \lesssim_{n, p, q} \|u_0\|_{L^q_x}.
            \end{equation} 

        \item \textup{(Parabolic ``Strichartz").} For $2 \leq p \leq \infty$ and non-negative integers $n \in \mathbb N_0$ such that $(p, n) \neq (2, 0)$, 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:parabolic-strichartz}
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)} e^{s \Delta} u_0 \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}s} L^p_x}
                \lesssim_{n, p} \| u_0 \|_{L^2_x}. 
            \end{equation}

    \end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
The former is a standard consequence of Young's convolution inequality and the explicit form of the heat kernel. For the latter, when $p = 2$, parabolic smoothing reduces the estimate to showing the $n = 1$ case, which is precisely the parabolic energy estimate, c.f. (\ref{eq:abs-heat-energy}). For $2 < p \leq \infty$, it suffices to prove the result for $n = 0$ by parabolic smoothing. Then one can employ a $T$-$T^*$-argument, see \cite[Lemma 2.5]{Tao2009}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
Let $A$ be a connection $1$-form on $\mathbb R^2 \times [0, \infty)$ solving the Yang-Mills heat flow (\ref{eq:YMH}). Then for $2 \leq p \leq \infty$ and non-negative integers $n \in \mathbb N_0$,
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:F12-sobolev}
        \begin{split}
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)}  F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^p_x} 
                &\lesssim_{p, n} \bigl\|  \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x},\\
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)}  F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^p_x} 
                &\lesssim_{p, n} \bigl\|  \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}, \qquad (p, n) \neq (2, 0). 
        \end{split}
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
Let $A$ be a connection $1$-form on $\mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the Yang-Mills heat flow (\ref{eq:YMH}), and suppose that  
         \begin{equation}\label{eq:heat-data-0}
            {\bigl\| \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}}
                \leq \underline s^{-\frac12}.
        \end{equation}
    If $\mathsf U : \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s] \to \mathbb C$ is a sufficiently regular solution to the abstract linear parabolic equation (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-eq}), then we have the following estimates: 
    \begin{itemize}   
        \item \textup{(Energy estimate).} 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:abs-heat-energy}
            \bigl\| \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}  
                \lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s \, \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}.
        \end{equation}
        
        \item \textup{(Weighted energy estimate).} For each $\gamma > 0$, 
        \begin{equation}
             \big\| s^\gamma \mathsf U \big\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \big\| s^\gamma (s^{\frac12} \mathsf D) \mathsf U \big\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                \lesssim \gamma \big\|s^\gamma \mathsf U\big\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \big\| s^{\gamma + 1} \mathsf N \big\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}. \label{eq:abs-heat-weight}
        \end{equation}
        
        \item \textup{(Smoothing estimate).} For each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$,  
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:abs-smooth}
            \begin{split}
            \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)}  \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} &+ \bigl\|  (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n + 1)}  \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
                \lesssim_n \bigl\| \overline\mathsf U\bigr\|_{L^2_x} +  \bigl\| s (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(\leq n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}.
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}
       

        \item \textup{(Dyadic smoothing estimate).} For each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$ and $\gamma \in \mathbb R$, 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:dyadic-smooth}
            \bigl\| {s'}^\gamma ({s'}^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U (s') \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                \lesssim_n \bigl\| {s'}^\gamma \mathsf U (\tfrac12 s') \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s^{1 + \gamma} (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(\leq n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([\frac12 s', s'])}.
            \end{equation}
            
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Multiplying the abstract parabolic equation (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-eq}) by $\mathsf U$, integrating-by-parts on $\mathbb R^2$ yields the energy identity 
        \[
            \tfrac12 \partial_s\bigl\| \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 +  \bigl\| \mathsf D \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2  
                = \int_{\mathbb R^2} \mathsf N \cdot \mathsf U \, dx.
        \]
    Cauchy-Schwarz allows us to bound the second term on the right by $\| \mathsf N \|_{L^2_x} \| \mathsf U \|_{L^2_x}$. Integrating in $s$ on the interval $[0, s']$ and taking supremum over $s' \in [0, \underline s]$ furnishes 
        \begin{align*}
            \tfrac12 \bigl\| \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}^2 + \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}^2 
                &\leq \tfrac12 \bigl\| \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 + \bigl\| s \, \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}  \bigl\| \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} .
        \end{align*}
    Interpolating, the third term on the right-hand side may be controlled by $\| s \mathsf N \|_{L^1_{ds/s} L^2_x}^2$, plus a term which can be absorbed into the left-hand side. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Commuting $s^\gamma$ into the abstract parabolic equation (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-eq}), 
        \[
            \big(\mathsf D_s - \mathsf D^j \mathsf D_j\big) (s^\gamma \mathsf U) 
                = \gamma s^{\gamma - 1} \mathsf U + s^\gamma \mathsf N.
        \]
    Multiplying by $s^\gamma \mathsf U$, integrating on $\mathbb R^2$, and integrating-by-parts furnishes the energy identity
        \[
            \tfrac12 \partial_s \big\|s^\gamma \mathsf U\big\|_{L^2_x}^2 + \frac1s \big\| s^\gamma (s^{\frac12} \mathsf D) \mathsf U \big\|_{L^2_x}^2 
                = \frac{\gamma}{s} \big\| s^\gamma \mathsf U \big\|_{L^2_x}^2 + \int_{\mathbb R^2} s^\gamma \mathsf N \cdot s^\gamma \mathsf U \, dx. 
        \]
    Cauchy-Schwartz allows us to bound the second term on the right by $\|s^\gamma \mathsf N\|_{L^2_x} \|s^\gamma \mathsf U\|_{L^2_x}$. Integrating in $s$ on the interval $[0, s']$ and taking supremum over $s' \in [0, \underline s]$ yields the inequality
        \begin{align*}
            \tfrac12 \big\|s^\gamma \mathsf U\big\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}^2 + \big\| s^\gamma (s^{\frac12} \mathsf D) \mathsf U \big\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}^2 
                &\leq \gamma \big\|s^\gamma \mathsf U\big\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}^2 + \big\| s^{\gamma + 1} \mathsf N \big\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \big\| s^\gamma \mathsf U \big\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}.
        \end{align*}
    Interpolating, the third term on the right-hand side may be controlled by $\|s^{\gamma + 1} \mathsf N\|^2_{L^1_{ds/s} L^2_x}$ plus a term which can be absorbed by the first term on the left-hand side. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
We will consider the case $\mathsf D_{\bf a} = {\bf D}_{\bf a}$; the case $\mathsf D_{\bf a} = \partial_{\bf a}$ follows a similar but easier argument due to the lack of commutator terms. For brevity, denote $\mathrm E_{n}$ for the energy-type quantity, and $\mathrm B_{n}$ for the bulk-type quantity, 
        \begin{align*}
            \mathrm E_{n} 
                &:= \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n - 1)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}, \\
                \mathrm B_{n} 
                &:= \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}.
        \end{align*}
    Observe the $n = 0$ case is precisely the energy estimate (\ref{eq:abs-heat-energy}). Proceeding inductively, we assume 
        \[
            \mathrm{E}_b + \mathrm{B}_b 
                \lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq b)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
        \]
    for $b = 0, \dots, n$. Applying the weighted energy estimate (\ref{eq:abs-heat-weight}) with $\gamma = \frac{n}{2}$ to the equation for the $n$-th order derivatives (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-eq-n})
        \begin{align*}
            \mathrm E_{n + 1} + \mathrm B_{n + 1}
                &\lesssim \mathrm B_{n} + \bigl\| s (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \sum_{\substack{a + b = n \\ b \neq 0}} \bigl\| s (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} F_{12} \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}\\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \sum_{\substack{a + b = n \\ b \neq 0}} \underline s^\frac12 \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s, x}} \cdot \mathrm{B}_{b} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} ,
        \end{align*}
    using H\"older to estimate the commutator terms, and the inductive hypotheses for the bulk terms, parabolic smoothing of the magnetic field (\ref{eq:F12-sobolev}) and (\ref{eq:heat-data-0}).
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Since $s' \sim s$ in the interval $s \in [\frac12 s', s']$, it suffices to show the result for $\gamma = 0$. Denoting heat-temporal translation by $\tfrac12 s'$ with tildes, e.g.
            \begin{align*}
                \widetilde \mathsf U (s) 
                    &:= \mathsf U (\tfrac12 s' + s),\\
                \widetilde \mathsf N (s) 
                    &:= \mathsf N (\tfrac12 s' + s), 
            \end{align*}
        we apply the abstract parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:abs-smooth}) to $\widetilde \mathsf U$ on the interval $[0, \tfrac12 s']$. On the left hand-side of the inequality, we have 
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl\| ({s'}^\frac12 \mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf U (s') \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    \lesssim \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \widetilde\mathsf D)^{(n)} \widetilde\mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x ([0, \frac12 s'])} .
            \end{align*}
    On the right-hand side, it is convenient to first convert from the scale-invariant measure $\frac{ds}{s}$ to the translation-invariant measure $ds$. Applying Cauchy-Schwarz and observing that $s \sim s'$ within $s \in [\tfrac12 s', s']$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s (s^\frac12 \widetilde\mathsf D)^{(n)} \widetilde \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([0, \frac12 s'])}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| s^{\frac{n}{2}} \bigr\|_{L^2_{s} ([0, \frac12 s'])} \bigl\| \mathsf D^{(n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^2_{s, x} ([\frac12 s', s'])} \\
                &\lesssim |s'|^{\frac{n + 1}{2}} \bigl\| \mathsf D^{(n)} \mathsf D \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^2_{s, x} ([\frac12 s', s'])}  \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| s (s^\frac12\mathsf D)^{(n)} \mathsf D \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([\frac12 s', s'])} .
        \end{align*}
    Collecting these observations gives the desired inequality.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:diff-smooth}
    Let $A$ and $A'$ be connection $1$-forms on $\mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the Yang-Mills heat flow (\ref{eq:YMH}) in caloric gauge (\ref{eq:caloric-prelim}) with heat-temporal initial data satisfying (\ref{eq:heat-data-0}), and suppose that $\mathsf U, \mathsf U' : \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s] \to \mathbb C$ solve respective abstract linear parabolic equations (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-eq}) and satisfy the bounds
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:U-diff-K}
            \bigl\| s^\frac18 (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\| s^\frac18 (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf U' \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}  
                \lesssim_n \mathcal K,
        \end{equation}
    for some $\mathcal K > 0$. Then 
        \begin{equation}
        \begin{split}
            \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} &+ \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n + 1)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}\\
                    &\lesssim \bigl\| \delta \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \bigl\| s \, \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                    &\qquad +  \underline s^\frac18 \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} + \underline s^\frac14 \cdot \bigl\| \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \cdot \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} + \underline s^\frac14 \cdot \bigl\| \nabla \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^2_x}\Bigr).
        \end{split}
        \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Define the $\mathrm{E}_n$ the energy-type quantity, $\mathrm{B}_n$ and $\widetilde{\mathrm{B}}_n$ for the bulk-type quantities,
        \begin{align*}
            \delta \mathrm{E}_n 
                &:= \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n - 1)} \mathsf U  \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x},\\
            \delta \mathrm{B}_n  
                &:= \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n - 1)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x},\\
            \delta \widetilde{\mathrm{B}}_n 
                &:= \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} ,
        \end{align*}
    Commuting $\delta$ with ${\bf D}$ a l\'a (\ref{eq:commute-diff}), applying H\"older, interpolation from Lemma \ref{lem:interpolate} with (\ref{eq:U-diff-K}),
        \begin{align*}
            \delta \widetilde{\mathrm{B}_n} 
                &\lesssim \delta\mathrm{B}_n + \bigl\| [s^\frac12 {\bf D}, \delta] (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n - 1)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \delta\mathrm{B}_n + \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n - 1)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^4_x} \\
                &\lesssim \delta \mathrm{B}_n + \underline s^\frac18 \cdot \mathcal K \cdot  \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x}.
        \end{align*}
    This will be useful on the left. Next, we estimate the terms on the right of (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-diff}); the first term consists of commutators with the covariant Laplacian, so expanding via the identity (\ref{eq:commute-diff-laplace}), applying H\"older and the assumption (\ref{eq:U-diff-K}) appropriately, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s \cdot s^{\frac{n}{2}}\cdot \mathrm{I}_n \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n + 1)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^4_x} +  \Bigl( \bigl\| \delta \partial^\ell \overline A_\ell \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \bigl\| \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \Bigr) \bigl\| s(s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s, x}} \\
                &\lesssim \underline s^\frac18 \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} + \underline s^{\frac38} \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\| \delta \partial^\ell \overline A_\ell \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \Bigr).
        \end{align*}
    The second term consists of differences falling on the magnetic field. Applying parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:F12-sobolev}) and the assumption (\ref{eq:U-diff-K}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s \cdot s^{\frac{n}{2}} \cdot\mathrm{II}_n \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim  \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(\leq n)} \delta F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^\infty_x} \cdot \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \underline s^{\frac38} \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \bigl\| \delta \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
        \end{align*}
    The third term consists of differences falling on derivatives of $\mathsf U$. By Cauchy-Schwarz and the assumption (\ref{eq:heat-data-0}) on $\overline F_{12}$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\|  s \cdot s^{\frac{n}{2}} \cdot \mathrm{III}_n \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \sum_{\substack{a + b = n \\ b \neq 0}} \underline s^\frac12 \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s, x}} \cdot \delta \widetilde{\mathrm{B}}_b \\
                &\lesssim \sum_{b = 1}^n \delta \widetilde{\mathrm{B}}_b.
        \end{align*}
    
    Armed with the previous calculations, we now apply the energy estimate (\ref{eq:abs-heat-energy}) to the difference equation (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-diff}) with $n = 0$,
        \begin{align*}
            \delta\mathrm{E}_1 + \delta\mathrm{B}_1
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \delta \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s \cdot (\mathrm{I}_0 + \mathrm{II}_0) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \bigl\| s \, \delta \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \delta \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  +  \underline s^\frac18 \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \bigl( 1 + \underline s^\frac12 \bigl\| \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \bigr) \cdot \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} + \underline s^{\frac38} \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \bigl\| \nabla \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s \, \delta \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} .
        \end{align*}
    Recall $\delta \widetilde{\mathrm B}_1$ can be controlled by $\delta \mathrm B_1$, so the result for $n = 0$ holds. Proceeding inductively, we assume the result holds up to $n$. Applying the abstract weighted energy estimte (\ref{eq:abs-heat-weight}) with $\gamma = \tfrac{n}{2}$ to (\ref{eq:abstract-heat-diff}), 
        \begin{align*}
             \delta\mathrm{E}_{n + 1} + \delta\mathrm{B}_{n + 1} 
                &\lesssim \delta \widetilde{\mathrm{B}}_n + \bigl\| s \cdot s^\frac{n}{2} \cdot (\mathrm{I}_n + \mathrm{II}_n + \mathrm{III}_n ) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \bigl\| s \cdot \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \delta \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  +  \underline s^\frac18 \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \bigl( 1 + \underline s^\frac12 \bigl\| \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \bigr) \cdot \bigl\| \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^4_x} + \underline s^{\frac38} \cdot \mathcal K \cdot \bigl\| \nabla \delta \overline A \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s \, \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} \mathsf N \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} ,
        \end{align*}
    using the inductive hypothesis to handle the appearance of the bulk term on the right. As $\delta \widetilde{\mathrm B}_{n + 1}$ can be controlled by $\delta \mathrm{B}_n$, we can complete the induction.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
The choice $s^{1/8}$ in the assumption (\ref{eq:U-diff-K}) is a bit arbitrary. Similarly, we could have replaced $\nabla \delta A$ in $L^2$ with the weaker quantity
        \[
            \|s^\frac14 \delta \nabla A \|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}
        \]
    on the right-hand side. The point is that when commuting $\delta$ through the equation, there is quite a bit of room in terms of powers of $s$.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration obeying the covariant heat equation (\ref{eq:covariant-heat})-(\ref{eq:covariant-heat2}). Then the following parabolic equations hold for
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item the (spatially) differentiated scalar field:
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Dphi-heat}
            \big({\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \big)  {\bf D} \phi
                = F_{12} \cdot{\bf D} \phi,
            \end{equation}

        \item the covariant Hessian:
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Dphi-heat-2}
                \bigl( {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \bigr) {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi
                    = F_{12} \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi + \nabla F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi,
            \end{equation}

        \item the charge density: 
            \begin{align}
                (\partial_s - \Delta) \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2) 
                &= {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi ,\label{eq:charge-heat}
            \end{align}

        \item the Gauss tension field:
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Gauss-heat-prelim}
                (\partial_s - \Delta) \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, 
                    = {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi.
            \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item This is an immediate consequence of the commutator identity (\ref{eq:parabolic-commute}).
        
        \item This is an immediate consequence of the commutator identity (\ref{eq:parabolic-commute}) and the product rule. 

        \item By the covariant heat equation (\ref{eq:covariant-heat}) and product rule (\ref{eq:product}),
            \begin{align*}
                \partial_s \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2) 
                    &= - \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi \cdot {\bf D}_s \phi) \\
                    &= - \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \phi) \\
                    &= \Delta \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2) + |{\bf D} \phi|^2.
            \end{align*}

        \item Subtracting the equations for the magnetic field (\ref{eq:F12-heat}) and the charge density (\ref{eq:charge-heat}) gives the result. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $\mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the covariant heat equation (\ref{eq:covariant-heat})-(\ref{eq:covariant-heat2}) such that $(\overline A, \overline \phi) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$. Then for each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$ and $2 \leq p \leq \infty$, we have: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Parabolic smoothing for ${\bf D} \phi$).} 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:Dphi-sobolev}
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^p_x} + \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n + 1)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^p_x} 
                \lesssim_{n} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}.
        \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Parabolic Strichartz estimate for ${\bf D} \phi$).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}
            \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} {\bf D} \phi  \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^p_x}
                \lesssim_p \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}, \qquad p \neq 2.
            \end{equation}

         \item \textup{(Gauss tension field parabolic smoothing).} 
            \begin{equation} \label{eq:Gauss-sobolev}
                \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)} \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^p_x} +  \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n + 1)} \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^p_x}
                    \lesssim_n \bigl\| \nabla \overline \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2.
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Uniform Gauss tension field bound).} 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Gauss-Linfty}
                \| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^\infty_{s, x}}
                    \lesssim \bigl\| \overline \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2.
            \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
By the interpolation Lemma \ref{lem:interpolate}, it suffices to prove the case $p = 2$. We compute the derivatives of the right-hand side of the equation (\ref{eq:Dphi-heat}) for ${\bf D} \phi$, 
        \[
            (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:Dphi-heat})}) 
                = \sum_{a + b = n} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} F_{12} \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} {\bf D} \phi.
        \]
       Then, by H\"older, parabolic smoothing for the magnetic field (\ref{eq:F12-sobolev}), and the assumption on the heat-temporal initial data $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$,
         \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:Dphi-heat})}) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \sum_{a + b \leq n} \underline s^\frac12 \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s, x}} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)}  {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}\\
                &\lesssim \underline s^{\frac12} \bigl\| \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \varepsilon \cdot \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} ,
            \end{align*}
    Inserting the calculation above into the abstract smoothing estimate (\ref{eq:abs-smooth}) applied to the equation (\ref{eq:Dphi-heat}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi}\bigr\|_{L^2_x} +  \bigl\| s \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:Dphi-heat})}) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim  \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi}\bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \varepsilon \cdot \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}.
        \end{align*}
    If $\varepsilon_n \ll 1$, then the second term on the right may be absorbed into the left-hand side.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Applying the maximum principle (\ref{eq:maximum-principle}) to the equation (\ref{eq:Dphi-heat}) for ${\bf D} \phi$ gives
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi (s)\bigr\|_{L^p_x} 
                    &\leq \bigl\| e^{s \Delta} | \overline{{\bf D} \phi} | \bigr\|_{L^p_x} + \int_0^s  \Big\| e^{(s - s') \Delta} |F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi| (s') \Big\|_{L^p_x} \, ds'  \\
                    &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \Bigl\|\int_0^s  \Big\| e^{(s - s') \Delta} |F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi| (s') \Big\|_{L^p_x} \, ds' \Bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}}},
            \end{align*}
        Multiplying by $s^{1/2 - 1/p}$ and taking $L^2_{ds/s}$, we estimate the homogeneous flow by parabolic Strichartz (\ref{eq:parabolic-strichartz}),
            \[
                \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} e^{s \Delta} |\overline{{\bf D} \phi}| \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^p_x}
                    \lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
            \]
        For the inhomogeneous flow, we apply the $(L^2 \to L^p)$-smoothing estimate (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) and the parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:F12-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) to obtain 
            \begin{align*}
                \Bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} \int_0^s  \Big\| e^{(s - s') \Delta} |F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi| (s') \Big\|_{L^p_x} \, ds' \Bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}}}
                    &\lesssim \Bigl\|   \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s}{s - s'}\Bigr)^{\frac12 - \frac1p} \, \bigl\| F_{12} (s') \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi(s') \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \, ds' \Bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}}} \\
                    &\lesssim  \Bigl\| \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s}{s - s'}\Bigr)^{\frac12 - \frac1p} |s'|^{\frac12} \, \bigl\| \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \,  \frac{ds'}{s'} \Bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}}}\\
                    &\lesssim \underline s^\frac12 \bigl\| \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                    &\lesssim\bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
            \end{align*}
    recalling the size of the heat-temporal initial data $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$ in the last line.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
By the interpolation Lemma \ref{lem:interpolate}, it suffices to prove the case $p = 2$. We compute the derivatives of the right-hand side of the equation (\ref{eq:Gauss-heat-prelim}) for $\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,$ using the product rule (\ref{eq:product}), 
        \[
            (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)} \nabla (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:Gauss-heat-prelim})})
                = \sum_{a + b = n} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)} {\bf D} \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} {\bf D} \phi. 
        \]  
    Then, by H\"older, parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and parabolic Strichartz (\ref{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\|s \cdot  (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(\leq n)} \nabla (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:Gauss-heat-prelim})}) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \sum_{a + b \leq n} \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^\infty_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} {\bf D} \phi\bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2.
        \end{align*}
    Inserting this calculation into the abstract smoothing estimate (\ref{eq:abs-smooth}) applied to (\ref{eq:Gauss-heat-prelim}) gives (\ref{eq:Gauss-sobolev}).
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Estimating Duhamel's formula to the equation for the Gauss tension field (\ref{eq:Gauss-heat-prelim}) in $L^\infty_x$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, (s) \|_{L^\infty_x}
                &\lesssim \|  \overline\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^\infty_x} + \int_0^s \| {s'}^\frac12 {\bf D} \phi (s') \|_{L^\infty_x}^2 \, \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                &\lesssim \| \overline \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^\infty_x} + \| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \|_{L^2_x}^2,
        \end{align*}
    using the parabolic Strichartz estimate (\ref{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}) in the second line.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
To illustrate some analogies with the standard Littlewood-Paley theory, one should compare the smoothing estimates (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) to the Sobolev-Bernstein estimates, c.f. \cite[Appendix A]{Tao2006}, and the parabolic Strichartz bound (\ref{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}) with the Sobolev embedding 
        \[
            \dot H^1 (\mathbb R^2) \hookrightarrow \dot B^{-2/p, p}_2 (\mathbb R^2) ,
        \]
    under the interpretation that $(s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi (s)$ is localised to medium frequencies $s^{-1/2}$.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $\mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the covariant heat equation (\ref{eq:covariant-heat})-(\ref{eq:covariant-heat2}) such that $(\overline A, \overline \phi) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$. Then we have the following bounds:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item \textup{(Charge density bound).} 
                \begin{equation}\label{eq:charge-sobolev}
                    \big\| 1 - |\phi|^2 \big\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} 
                        \lesssim \big\| 1 - |\overline\phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x} + \big\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \big\|_{L^2_x}.
                \end{equation}
                
            \item \textup{(Brezis-Gallou\"et-type bound).} For any $s_1 < s_2$, 
                \begin{equation}\label{eq:brezis-0}
                    \bigl\| \phi(s_1) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} 
                        \lesssim \bigl\| \phi(s_2) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{s_2}{s_1} \Bigr) \cdot \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}.
                \end{equation}
            In particular, 
                \begin{align}\label{eq:brezis}
                    \bigl\|\phi (s) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{x}}
                        &\lesssim \underline s^{-\frac12} \Bigl( 1 + \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s} \Bigr) \Bigr)   .
                \end{align}
            and, for any $\gamma > 0$, 
                \begin{align}\label{eq:inefficient-smooth}
                    \bigl\| s^\gamma \phi(s) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s, x}} 
                        \lesssim \underline s^{\gamma - \frac12}. 
                \end{align}
        \end{itemize}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We estimate the right-hand side of the equation (\ref{eq:charge-heat}), 
        \begin{align*}
        \bigl\| s \cdot \text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:charge-heat})} \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
            &\lesssim \bigl\| s^\frac12 \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}}} \bigl\| s^\frac14 {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^4_x}^2 \\
            &\lesssim \underline s^\frac12 \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 \\
            &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}, 
        \end{align*}
    using smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) in the second line and the size of the heat-temporal initial data $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$ in the third line. The estimate (\ref{eq:charge-sobolev}) follows from the energy estimate (\ref{eq:abs-heat-energy}) applied to the equation (\ref{eq:charge-heat}).
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Rewriting $|\phi|$ using the fundamental theorem of calculus in $s$ and using the diamagnetic inequality (\ref{eq:diamagnetic}), 
        \begin{align*}
            |\phi(s_1)|  
                \leq |\phi(s_2)| + \int_{s_1}^{s_2} |s {\bf D}_s \phi(s)| \frac{ds}{s}.
        \end{align*}
    For the ``high-frequency'' part, we use parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and Cauchy-Schwarz, 
        \begin{align*}
             \int_{s_1}^{s_2} \|s {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi(s)\|_{L^\infty_s} \frac{ds}{s}
                &\lesssim \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{s_2}{s_1} \Bigr) \bigl\| s^\frac12 ({s}^\frac12 {\bf D}) {\bf D} \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s} } L^\infty_x} \\
                &\lesssim  \underline s^{-\frac12}  \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{s_2}{s_1} \Bigr) .
        \end{align*}
    This proves (\ref{eq:brezis-0}). 
    
    For (\ref{eq:brezis}), take $s_1 = s$ and $s_2 = \underline s$; we estimate the ``low-frequency'' part using the Sobolev-type estimate (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}) and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and the charge density bound (\ref{eq:charge-sobolev}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\|\underline \phi\bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} 
                &\lesssim  1 + \bigl\| 1 - |\underline \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^\frac13 \bigl\| \underline {\bf D}^{(2)} \underline\phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac13} \\
                &\lesssim \underline s^{-\frac12}, 
        \end{align*}
    recalling the size of $\underline s^{-1}$ in the second line. 

    Multiplying (\ref{eq:brezis}) by $s^\gamma$ and recalling basic calculus, one easily sees (\ref{eq:inefficient-smooth}).
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a sufficiently regular configuration on $\mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the covariant heat equation (\ref{eq:covariant-heat})-(\ref{eq:covariant-heat2}) such that $(\overline A, \overline \phi) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$. Then, for each positiver integer $n \in \mathbb N$, we have the following bounds, 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Higher-order covariant derivative energy estimate).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Dphi-sobolev-high}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) {\bf D}^{(n)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                \lesssim  \bigl\| \overline{\bf D}^{(n)} \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} .
        \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Higher-order Gauss tension field energy estimate).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-sobolev-high}
            \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}
                \lesssim \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \nabla \overline \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} +  \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \Bigl(\bigl\| \overline{\bf D}^{(n)} \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \overline F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}\Bigr) .
        \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Writing the equations (\ref{eq:F12-heat}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-heat}) for $\mathsf U = \{ F_{12}, {\bf D} \phi\}$ schematically, it follows from the product rule and the commutator identity (\ref{eq:commute}) that 
        \[
            (\mathsf D_s - \mathsf D^\ell \mathsf D_\ell) \mathsf D^{(n)} \mathsf U 
                = \sum_{a + b = n} \mathsf D^{(a)} \mathsf U \cdot \mathsf D^{(b)}\mathsf U. 
        \]
    Applying the abstract energy estimate (\ref{eq:abs-heat-energy}) to the equation above, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \mathsf D^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\|  (s^\frac12 \mathsf D)\mathsf D^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf D^{(n)} \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \sum_{a + b = n} \bigl\| s \, \mathsf D^{(a)} \mathsf U \cdot \mathsf D^{(b)} \mathsf U  \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}\\ 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf D^{(n)} \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \sum_{a + b = n} \underline s^{\frac12} \bigl\| s^{\frac{a}{2n}}\mathsf D^{(a)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^{2n/a}_x} \bigl\| s^{\frac{b}{2n}} \mathsf D^{(b)} \mathsf U  \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^{2n/b}_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf D^{(n)} \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \underline s^{\frac12} \Bigl( \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \mathsf D) \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\| s^\frac12 \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s, x}} \Bigr) \bigl\| \mathsf D^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline \mathsf D^{(n)} \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \underline s^{\frac12} \bigl\| \overline \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \mathsf D^{(n)} \mathsf U \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x},
        \end{align*}
    applying H\"older in the second line, interpolating appropriately in the third line, and the parabolic smoothing estimates (\ref{eq:F12-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) in the last line.
