                &= 2\int_{s_1}^{s_2} \int_{s"}^{s_2} \Bigl\langle ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(2)} {\bf D} \phi (s') , ({s"}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(2)} {\bf D} \phi (s")\Bigr\rangle_{L^2_x} \frac{ds'}{s'} \frac{ds"}{s"} 
        \end{align*}
    using symmetry to write this as an integral on $s" < s'$. Then by Lemma \ref{lem:orthogonal},
        \begin{align*}
            \Bigl\| \int_{s_1}^{s_2} ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(2)} {\bf D}\phi (s') \, \frac{ds'}{s'}  \Bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2
                &\lesssim \bigl\| ({s}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(3)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_1, s_2])} \bigl\| ({s}^\frac12 {\bf D}) {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_1, s_2])} \overset{|s_1 - s_2| \to 0}{\longrightarrow} 0,
        \end{align*}
    concluding convergence via parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and the monotone convergence theorem.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:smooth-data}
    Let $(A, \phi) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$ be a finite-energy configuration. Then there exists a sequence $\{ ({A}^{[n]}, {{\vphantom{A}\phi}}^{[n]}) \}_n \subseteq \mathfrak E^\infty$ of smooth configurations satisfying:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Uniform energy bounds).}
            \[
                ({ A}^{[n]}, {{\vphantom{A}\phi}}^{[n]})
                    \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)
            \]
        
        \item \textup{(Uniform Gauss tension field bounds).}
            \[
               \lim_{n \to \infty}\| {\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,}^{[n]} \|_{L^\infty_x}
                    \leq \| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^\infty_x}.
            \]


        \item \textup{(Convergence in $\mathfrak E$).}
            \[
                \lim_{n \to \infty} \operatorname*{dist}_\mathfrak E \bigl( ({A}^{[n]}, {{\vphantom{A}\phi}}^{[n]}), ({A}, {{\vphantom{A}\phi}}) \bigr) = 0.  
            \]
    \end{itemize}
    Furthermore, if $(A, \phi)$ satisfies the Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}), then $\{ ({A}^{[n]}, {{\vphantom{A}\phi}}^{[n]}) \}_n$ also satisfy the Coulmb gauge.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi) \in \mathpzc{E}^1 ([0, \underline s])$ be the $\mathfrak E$-caloric extension of $(A, \phi)$, and set 
        \[
             ({A}^{[n]}, {{\vphantom{A}\phi}}^{[n]})
                := (A, \phi)_{|s = \frac1n}, \qquad n \gg 1.
        \]
    The covariant estimates from Section \ref{subsec:LP-sobolev} imply that these are smooth configurations and the Gauss tension field is uniformly bounded. Furthermore, by Proposition \ref{prop:cts-s}, we have convergence of the $\mathfrak E$-metric, and, since $\mathfrak E(\underline s)$ is characterised by an open condition, this sequence can be chosen to reside in $\mathfrak E(\underline s)$. Since the curl-free part of the magnetic potential is transported (\ref{eq:A-transport}), the Coulomb gauge condition is also propagated. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:smooth-1}
    We say that a configuration $(A, \phi)$ on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ is a \textit{smooth solution} to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation if it solves (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}) and satisfies the following regularity properties:
    \begin{itemize} 
        \item The configuration $(A_x(t), \phi(t)) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ is smooth for each $t \in [0, T]$, and obeys the uniform bounds
            \[
                \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \mathcal E^N [A_x(t), \phi(t)] 
                    < \infty, \qquad \text{for each $N \in \mathbb N$.}
            \]

        \item It forms a continuous flow into the space of finite-energy configurations, $(A_x, \phi) \in C_t ([0, T] \to \mathfrak E)$. 
        
        \item The electromagnetic potential has regularity $A_t, \nabla A_x \in C^\infty_t H^\infty_x ([0, T] \times \mathbb R^2)$. 
        
        \item The scalar field has regularity $\phi \in C^\infty_{t, x} ([0, T] \times \mathbb R^2)$. 
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:smooth-LWP}
    Let $(A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ be a smooth configuration on $\mathbb R^2$ in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}), then there exists $T \equiv T(\mathcal E^{9000} [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}]) > 0$ and a smooth solution $(A, \phi)$ on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}) in DeTurck gauge (\ref{eq:DeTurck}) with initial data $(A, \phi)_{|t = 0} = (A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}})$. Furthermore, the solution obeys the following properties: 
    \begin{itemize}        
        \item \textup{(Covariant energy estimates).} For each positive integer $N \in \mathbb N$, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:EN-bound-1}
            \frac{d}{dt} \mathcal E^N [A, \phi] 
                \lesssim_N \mathcal C[A, \phi] \cdot \mathcal E^N [A, \phi].
        \end{equation}  

        \item \textup{(Continuation criterion).} The solution can be extended to a smooth solution on $[0, T^+]\times \mathbb R^2$ solving the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation for some $T^+ > T$ whenever 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:high-blow-up}
            \int_0^T \mathcal C[A(t), \phi(t)] \, dt  
                < \infty.
        \end{equation}
        
        \item \textup{(Conservation of energy and degree).} The abelian Higgs energy and topological degree are conserved by the flow, i.e. for all $t \in [0, T]$, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:high-conserve}
            \mathcal E_{\textup{AH}}[A(t), \phi(t)] 
                = \mathcal E_{\textup{AH}} [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}],
        \end{equation}
        and 
        \begin{equation}
            \deg [A(t), \phi(t)] 
                = \deg [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}].
        \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:control}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}). Then there exists $T_* \equiv T_* (\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,^{\mathrm{in}} \|_{L^\infty \cap H^1}, \mathcal E_{\textup{AH}} [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}]) > 0$ such that if $J \subseteq [0, T]$ is a sub-interval of length $|J| \leq T_*$, then
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:control-bound}
            \int_J \mathcal C[A(t), \phi(t)] \, dt 
                \leq 2. 
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:global-1}
    Let $(A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ be a smooth configuration on $\mathbb R^2$ in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}). Then there exists a smooth solution $(A, \phi)$ on $[0, \infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}) in DeTurck gauge (\ref{eq:DeTurck}) with the initial data $(A, \phi)_{|t = 0} = (A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}})$. 
    
    Furthermore, for each positive integer $N \in \mathbb N$, the solution obeys the covariant energy estimate 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:EN-bound-2}
            \mathcal E^N [A (t), \phi (t)] 
                \leq \mathcal E^N [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}] \exp (\kappa t),
        \end{equation} 
    for some constant $\kappa \equiv \kappa(N, \| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,^{\mathrm{in}} \|_{L^\infty \cap H^1}, \mathcal E_{\textup{AH}} [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}])$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:abs-schro-energy}
    Let $A$ be a connection $1$-form on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$, and $\mathsf V : [0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R$ a real-valued potential. Then for sufficiently regular solutions $u : [0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb C$ to the electromagnetic Schr\"odinger equation,
        \[
            \big(i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j + \mathsf V \big) u
                = \mathsf N,
        \]
    the following energy estimate holds, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-energy}
            \frac{d}{dt} \| u \|_{L^2_x}^2
                \leq \| u \|_{L^2_x} \| \mathsf N \|_{L^2_x}. 
        \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
By the product rule (\ref{eq:product}) and integration-by-parts, 
        \begin{align*}
            \frac{d}{dt} \| u \|_{L^2_x}^2
                &= \langle u, {\bf D}_t u \rangle_{L^2_x}\\
                &= \langle u , i ({\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j + \mathsf V) u \rangle_{L^2_x} - \langle u, i \mathsf N \rangle_{L^2_x} \\
                &= \langle u, - i \mathsf N \rangle_{L^2_x}.
        \end{align*}
    We conclude (\ref{eq:abstract-energy}) by Cauchy-Schwarz.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:higher-schrodinger}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a solution to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}). Then for each positive integer $n \in \mathbb N$, we have the following schematic equation, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:higher-schrodinger}
        \begin{split}
            \Bigl(i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi 
                &= {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi + \sum_{a + b + c = n} {\bf D}^{(a)} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(b)} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(c)} \phi\\
                &\qquad + \sum_{a + b = n} \nabla^{(a)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \cdot {\bf D}^{(b)} \phi .
        \end{split}
        \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
We have the commutator identity
        \begin{align*}
            \Bigl[{\bf D}, i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j + \tfrac\lambda2(1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr] 
                &= F_{tx} + F_{12} \cdot {\bf D}  + \nabla F_{12}  + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi \\
                &= F_{12} \cdot {\bf D}  + \nabla F_{12}  + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi\\
                &= {\bf D} + \phi \cdot \phi \cdot {\bf D} + \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \cdot {\bf D} + \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi
        \end{align*}
    using the basic commutator identities (\ref{eq:commute}), (\ref{eq:laplace-commute}) in the first line, and writing Amp\'ere law's schematically as $F_{tx} = \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \nabla F_{12}$ in the second line, and re-expressing the magnetic field using the Gauss tension field and charge density in the third line. The desired equation (\ref{eq:higher-schrodinger}) then follows from an inductive application of the product rule and the commutator identity above.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:aprioriestimate}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}). Then for each positive integer $n \in \mathbb N$, we have 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:energyestimate}
        \begin{split}
            \frac{d}{dt} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 
                &\lesssim_n \mathcal C[A, \phi] \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 + \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2  \Bigr).
        \end{split}
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Applying the abstract energy estimate (\ref{eq:abstract-energy}) to the covariant Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:higher-schrodinger}), it remains to estimate the right-hand side of the equation in $L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$. The linear term can be estimated immediately. For the non-linear terms, heuristically, the worst terms on the right-hand side of the equation (\ref{eq:higher-schrodinger}) are the interactions with ``unbalanced" derivatives, namely 
    \[
        \phi \cdot \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi ,\qquad \phi \cdot \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,, \qquad \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \cdot {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi , \qquad \phi \cdot \bigl( {\bf D}^{(a)} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(b)} \phi\bigr) ,
    \]
    where $a, b \neq 0$. We estimate each term by $L^\infty \times L^2 \to L^2$, and the magnetic interpolation inequality (\ref{eq:GN-interpolation}) for the last term, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \text{unbalanced} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \Bigl( \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} +  \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}^2  \Bigr) \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                    &\qquad + \sum_{\substack{a + b = n \\ a, b \neq 0}} \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(a)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/a}_x} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(b)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/b}_x}  \\
                &\lesssim \mathcal C[A, \phi] \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \Bigr).
        \end{align*}
    When the derivatives are instead ``balanced'', namely the terms 
        \begin{align*}
            {\bf D}^{(a)} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(b)}  \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(c)} \phi , \qquad \nabla^{(a)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \cdot {\bf D}^{(b)} \phi, 
        \end{align*}
    where $a, b, c \neq 0$, we use H\"older's inequality, the magnetic interpolation inequality (\ref{eq:GN-interpolation}) and the usual Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation,
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \text{balanced}  \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \sum_{\substack{a + b + c = n \\ a, b, c \neq 0}}\bigl\| {\bf D}^{(a)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/a}_x} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(b)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/b}_x} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(c)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/c}_x} + \sum_{\substack{a + b = n \\ a, b \neq 0}}\bigl\| \nabla^{(a)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^{2n/a}_x} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(b)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/b}_x}  \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( \bigl\|\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}   + \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \Bigr) \Bigl( \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \Bigr).
        \end{align*}
   These are acceptable in view of the right-hand side of the energy estimate (\ref{eq:energyestimate}).
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:charge-density}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}), then 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:apriori-charge}
            \frac{d}{dt} \Bigl( \big\| 1 - |\phi|^2 \big\|_{L^2_x}^2 \Bigr)
                \lesssim \| \phi\|_{L^\infty_x}^2 \| {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^2_x}^2. 
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Differentiating the charge density in $t$, using the covariant Schr\"odinger equation, and integrating-by-parts appropriately, we obtain
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_t \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2)^2
                &= - (1 - |\phi|^2) \, \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_t \phi) \\
                &=  (1 - |\phi|^2) \operatorname{Im} (\overline \phi {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \phi) \\
                &= (1 - |\phi|^2) \, \partial^j \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) \\
                &= \partial^j \Bigl( (1 - |\phi|^2) \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) \Bigr) + \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^j \phi) \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi). 
        \end{align*}
    Integrating on $\mathbb R^2$ and applying the divergence theorem yields the differential inequality.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
One can view the top-order energy estimate (\ref{eq:energyestimate}) as propagating ``frequency-localisation", which effectively confers ``finite-speed of propagation'' for $\phi$ as a solution to a Schr\"odinger equation and thereby control over lower-order quantities such as the charge density as in (\ref{eq:apriori-charge}). It is instructive to compare with the estimates for the linear Schr\"odinger flow on Zhidkov spaces, c.f. \cite{Gallo2004} and \cite[Section 2.2]{Gerard2006}, which play a similar role in the well-posedness theory for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
The idea of using a geometric heat flow as a tool for smoothing out a geometric dispersive equation was introduced by Tao \cite{Tao2004} in his work on global regularity for wave maps from $\mathbb R^2$ to hyperbolic space. Various authors have successfully adopted the approach for other problems, e.g. Bejenaru-Ionescu-Kenig-Tataru \cite{BejenaruEtAl2011} for Schr\"odinger maps, Oh \cite{Oh2014a, Oh2015a}, Gavrus \cite{Gavrus2022}, and Oh-Tataru \cite{OhTataru2019, OhTataru2020, OhTataru2021, OhTataru2022} for the hyperbolic Yang-Mills equation, A reader familiar with the literature will note that our approach slightly differs from the traditional implementation, which would dictate that we use the abelian Higgs gradient flow as opposed to the covariant heat equation. Nevertheless, there do not seem to be any advantages to using the gradient flow for studying the well-posedness of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:smooth-dP}
    We say that a configuration $(A, \phi)$ on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ is a \textit{smooth solution} to the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation if it solves the system (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}) and satisfies the following regularity properties: 
    \begin{itemize}        
        \item The configuration $(A_x(t,s ), \phi(t,s)) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ is smooth for each $t \in [0, T]$ and $s \in [0, \underline s]$, and obeys the uniform bounds for each positive integer $N \in \mathbb N$,
            \[
                \sup_{s \in [0, \underline s]} \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \mathcal E^N [A_x(t,s), \phi(t, s)]
                    < \infty. 
            \]

        \item The heat-temporal initial data satisfies $(\overline A_x(t), \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi}(t)) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$ for each $t \in [0, T]$. Moreover, it forms a continuous flow into the space of finite-energy configurations, i.e. $(\overline A_x, \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \in C_t ([0, T] \to \mathfrak E(\underline s))$. 
        
        \item The gauge potential has regularity $A_t, A_s, \nabla A_x \in C^\infty_{t, s} H^\infty_x (\mathbb R^2)$. 
        
        \item The scalar field has regularity $\phi \in C^\infty_{t, x, s} ([0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s])$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:dP-exist}
    Let $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A} \phi})$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}) with Schr\"odinger-temporal initial data $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi})_{|t = 0} \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$. Then there exists a smooth solution $(A, \phi)$ on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ to the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}) with heat-temporal initial data $(A, \phi)_{s = 0} = (\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi})$.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Imposing the DeTurck gauge in $s$,  
        \[
            A_s 
                = \partial^\ell A_\ell,
        \]
    it follows from a straight-forward calculation that the dynamic Yang-Mills heat flow (\ref{eq:d-covariant-heat2}) reduces to the linear heat equation for the electromagnetic potential, 
        \[
            (\partial_s - \Delta) A_\mu 
                = 0.
        \]
    For each $t$, we first solve in $s$ for the electromagnetic potential, and then the electromagnetic heat equation for the scalar field (\ref{eq:d-covariant-heat}) with $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A} \phi})$ as heat-temporal initial data. Since $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A} \phi})$ is a smooth solution to (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}), we by definition know that $(\overline A, \overline{\vphantom{A} \phi}) \in C_t ([0, T] \to \mathfrak E)$ and, by conservation of the abelian Higgs energy and transport of the Gauss tension field, we have $(\overline A_x (t), \overline{\vphantom{A}\phi}(t)) \in \mathfrak E(\underline s)$ for all $t$. The ensuing configurations $(A_x (t, s), \phi(t, s)) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ arising from the dynamic covariant heat flow are smooth uniformly in $t$ and $s$ by virtue of the covariant energy estimates (\ref{eq:charge-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev-high}), (\ref{eq:gauss-sobolev-high}). The remaining desired regularity properties can easily be read-off from the equations of motion and the calculations from Appendix \ref{sec:smooth-configurations} -- we leave their verification to the reader.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
Another approach is to impose the caloric gauge and apply Lemma \ref{lem:lwp-heat}, which yields a solution to the covariant-heat equation (\ref{eq:covariant-heat})-(\ref{eq:covariant-heat2}) for each fixed $t$. From here, it would remain to construct the electric potential $A_t$, which can be done by formally solving the linear heat equation for the electric field (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}) and then the transport equation for $A_t$ arising from (\ref{eq:d-covariant-heat2}) in the caloric gauge.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}). The covariant Hessian satisfies the following covariant Schr\"odinger equation,
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ds-schrodinger}
            \begin{split}
                \bigl( i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \bigr) (s{\bf D}^{(2)}) \phi 
                    &= (s {\bf D}^{(2)}) \phi +  \phi \cdot \phi \cdot (s{\bf D}^{(2)}) \phi + \phi \cdot (s^\frac12{\bf D}) \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \\
                        &\qquad + \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 \nabla) s^\frac12 F_{tx} + (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \cdot s^\frac12 F_{tx} \\
                        &\qquad + \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(2)} F_{12} + (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 \nabla) F_{12} + (s {\bf D}^{(2)}) \phi \cdot F_{12}\\
                        &\qquad + (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(2)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\,. 
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}
    Furthermore, we have the following covariant heat equations for
        \begin{itemize}
            \item the electromagnetic field,
                \begin{equation}\label{eq:Fmunu-heat}
                    (\partial_s - \Delta) F_{\mu\nu} 
                        = 0,
                \end{equation}

            \item the Ampere tension field,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Amp-heat}
                (\partial_s - \Delta) \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\,
                    =  {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi + F_{12} \cdot \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi,
            \end{equation}
           
            \item the Schr\"odinger tension field,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:CSS-heat}
                \bigl( {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \bigr) \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\,
                    =  \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \nabla F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi + F_{tx} \cdot {\bf D} \phi.
            \end{equation}
        \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Applying ${\bf D}^{(2)}$ to the definition of the Schr\"odinger tension field, commuting covariant derivatives and applying the product rule (\ref{eq:product}) wherever appropriate, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl( i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \bigr) {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi 
                &= - \tfrac\lambda2(1 - |\phi|^2) {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi  + \phi \cdot \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi\\
                    &\qquad  + \Bigl[ i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j , {\bf D}^{(2)} \Bigr] \phi \\
                    &\qquad + {\bf D}^{(2)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\,.
        \end{align*}
    Using the commutator identities (\ref{eq:commute}), (\ref{eq:laplace-commute}), the commutator may be expressed as
        \begin{align*}
            \Bigl[ i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j , {\bf D}^{(2)} \Bigr] \phi
                &= \Bigl[ i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j , {\bf D} \Bigr] {\bf D}\phi + {\bf D} \Bigl[ i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j , {\bf D} \Bigr] \phi  \\
                &= F_{t x} \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \nabla F_{t x} \cdot \phi + F_{12} \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi + \nabla F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \nabla^{(2)} F_{12} \cdot \phi.
        \end{align*}
    Multiplying the equation by $s$ and distributing powers appropriately gives the desired equation.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
By the Bianchi identity (\ref{eq:bianchi}) and (\ref{eq:d-covariant-heat2}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_s F_{\mu\nu} 
                &= \partial_\mu F_{s\nu} - \partial_\nu F_{s\mu} \\
                &=\partial^\ell ( \partial_\mu F_{\ell \nu} - \partial_\nu F_{\ell \mu}) \\
                &= \Delta F_{\mu \nu}, 
        \end{align*}
    as desired.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Applying $\partial_s - \Delta$ to the definition of the Ampere tension field, 
        \begin{align*}
            (\partial_s - \Delta) \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\,_j 
                &= (\partial_s - \Delta) \bigl( F_{tj} + \varepsilon_{jk} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi) + \partial_j F_{12} \bigr)\\
                &= (\partial_s -\Delta) \varepsilon_{jk} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi),
        \end{align*}
    since the electromagnetic field satisfies the linear heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}). It remains to see whether the terms generated by the charge current are acceptable. Applying ${\bf D}_s$ to the charge current, and using the covariant heat equation (\ref{eq:d-covariant-heat}) and the equation for ${\bf D} \phi$ (\ref{eq:Dphi-heat}), we compute via the product rule (\ref{eq:product})
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_s \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi)
                &= \operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}_s \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi) + \operatorname{Im} (\overline \phi {\bf D}_s {\bf D}_j \phi) \\
                &= \operatorname{Im}\bigl( \overline{{\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi \bigr) + \operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline \phi {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell {\bf D}_j \phi \bigr) - 2 F\indices{_j^\ell} \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_\ell \phi) \\
                &= \Delta \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) - 2 \operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{{\bf D}^\ell \phi} {\bf D}_\ell {\bf D}_j \phi \bigr) - 2 F\indices{_j^\ell} \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_\ell \phi).
        \end{align*}
    These terms are all acceptable in view of the right-hand side of the equation (\ref{eq:Amp-heat}).
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Commuting ${\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell$ into the definition of the Schr\"odinger tension field, we see by virtue of (\ref{eq:d-covariant-heat}) that $\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\,$ obeys a covariant heat equation forced by the commutator between the covariant parabolic operator and covariant Schr\"odinger operator, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl( {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell \bigr) \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\,
                &= \Bigl[ {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell, i {\bf D}_t + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr] \phi  .
        \end{align*}
    Separating out the commutator by (bi-)linearity, we compute
        \begin{align*}
             \bigl[ {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell, i {\bf D}_t \bigr] \phi
                &= \bigl( F_{st} - \partial^\ell F_{\ell t} + F\indices{_t^\ell} {\bf D}_\ell  \bigr) \phi \\
                &= 2 F\indices{_t^\ell} \, {\bf D}_\ell \phi,\\
            \bigl[ {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell , {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \bigr]\phi
                &= -i \bigl( \partial^j F_{sj} + 2 F\indices{_s^j} {\bf D}_j \bigr) \phi \\
                &= - 2i \partial^\ell F\indices{_\ell^j} {\bf D}_j \phi, \\
            \bigl[ {\bf D}_s - {\bf D}^\ell {\bf D}_\ell, \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \bigr] \phi 
                &= \phi \, (\partial_s - \Delta) \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) - \partial^\ell \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \, {\bf D}_\ell \phi \\
                &= \phi \overline{{\bf D}^\ell \phi} {\bf D}_\ell \phi + \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^\ell \phi) {\bf D}_\ell \phi,
        \end{align*}
    using the parabolic commutator identity (\ref{eq:parabolic-commute}), the Laplacian commutator identity (\ref{eq:laplace-commute}) and (\ref{eq:d-covariant-heat2}) in the first two calculations, and recalling the equation for the charge density (\ref{eq:charge-heat}) in the last calculation. These terms are all acceptable in view of the right-hand side of the equation (\ref{eq:CSS-heat}).
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ to the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}). Then, for each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$ and $2 \leq p \leq \infty$, we have the following:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Magnetic field uniform bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:F12-Linfty}
                \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)} F_{12}  (s)\bigr\|_{L^\infty_{x}} 
                    \lesssim_n  \bigl\|  \phi (s)\bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}^2 + \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \underline s^{-1}.
            \end{equation}   

        \item \textup{(Magnetic field $L^p$-bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:nabla-F12-Lp}
                \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)} \nabla F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^p_x}
                    \lesssim_n \bigl\| \phi(s) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{x}} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \underline s^{-1}.
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Electric field $L^p$-bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Fmunu-Lp}
                 \bigl\| s^{\frac12 - \frac1p} (s^{\frac12} \nabla)^{(n)} F_{tx} (s) \bigr\|_{L^p_{x}}
                    \lesssim_n \bigl\| \phi(s) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{x}} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \underline s^{-1}. 
            \end{equation}

    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
It suffices to prove the bounds for $n = 0$ by parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) applied to the heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}) for the magnetic field. Recalling the definition of the Gauss tension field and its uniform bound (\ref{eq:Gauss-Linfty}),
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}
                &\lesssim 1 + \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}^2 + \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \\
                &\lesssim 1 + \bigl\|  \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}^2 + \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi}\bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2,
        \end{align*}
    which is of acceptable form.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
By parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) for the heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}), it suffices to prove the bounds for $n = 0$ and $p = 2$. Recalling the definition of the Gauss tension field,
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \nabla F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \nabla \overline \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2,
        \end{align*}
    by parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and the Gauss tension field smoothing (\ref{eq:Gauss-sobolev}). These terms are acceptable.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
By parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) for the heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}), it suffices to prove the bounds for $n = 0$ and $p = 2$. Recalling the definition of the Amp\'ere tension field,
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 F_{tx} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| F_{tx} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \nabla F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{x}} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \bigl\| \nabla \overline \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2
        \end{align*}
    by parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and the previous estimate (\ref{eq:nabla-F12-Lp}). The last two three terms are acceptable, so it remains to estimate the Amp\'ere tension field. We defer this to the subsequent Proposition \ref{prop:tension-env}, namely the envelope bound (\ref{eq:amp-env}). Choosing the frequency envelope as in, say, Proposition \ref{prop:env-stable}, would complete the proof by the slowly-varying property and finite-energy.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:tension-env}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ to the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}). Fix $t \in [0, T]$, and suppose that $\mathtt c(s) \in L^2_{ds/s} ([0, \underline s])$ is a $\mathfrak E$-frequency envelope for $(A (t), \phi(t))$. Then for each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$, we have the following:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Amp\'ere tension field bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:amp-env}
                \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, (t, s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                    \lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(s).
            \end{equation}
        
        \item \textup{(Electric field bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ftx-env}
                \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n + 1)} F_{tx} (t, s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                    \lesssim_n \Bigl( 1 + \bigl\| \phi(t, s) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \Bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s). 
            \end{equation}

         \item \textup{(Schr\"odinger tension field bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:css-env}
                \bigl\| s^{-\frac12} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\, (t, s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                    \lesssim_n \Bigl( \| \phi(t, s) \|_{L^\infty_x}  \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \underline s^{-1} \Bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s).
            \end{equation}
    
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
Using the equation (\ref{eq:Amp-heat}), we decompose the Amp\'ere tension field between a higher-order term and lower-order term, 
            \begin{align*}
                \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, 
                    := \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, + \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\,,
            \end{align*}
        where 
            \begin{align}
                \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\,
                    &:=  (\partial_s - \Delta)^{-1} ({\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi), \label{eq:amp-heat-1}\\ 
                \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\,
                    &:= (\partial_s - \Delta)^{-1} ( \phi \cdot F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi) \label{eq:amp-heat-2}.   
            \end{align}
        By the triangle inequality, it suffices to prove (\ref{eq:amp-env}) for these two terms. 
        
        We use Duhamel's formula, $(L^1 \to L^2)$-parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}), and H\"older, 
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl\| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                    &\lesssim \int_0^s \bigl\| e^{(s - s') \Delta}  ({\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi)\bigr\|_{L^2_x} ds' \\
                    &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s - s'}\Bigr)^\frac12 \bigl\| |s'|^\frac12 \cdot {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^1_x} \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                    &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s - s'}\Bigr)^\frac12 \cdot \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(s') \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                    &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s - s'}\Bigr)^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{s}{\, s'\,} \Bigr)^{\frac1{1000}} \cdot \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(s) \frac{ds'}{s'} \lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(s)
            \end{align*}
        using parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and the slowly-varying property. Similarly, 
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl\|\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    &\lesssim \int_0^s \bigl\| e^{(s - s') \Delta} (\phi \cdot F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi) \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \, ds' \\
                    &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac12 \bigl\| |s'|^\frac12 \cdot \phi \cdot F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^1_x} \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                    &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac12 |s'|^\frac13 \cdot \bigl\| |s'|^\frac16 \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \cdot \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(\underline s) \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                    &\lesssim  \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{s'}{\,\underline s\,} \Bigr)^\frac13 \cdot \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \Bigl( \frac{\,\underline s\,}{s} \Bigr)^{\frac1{1000}} \cdot \mathtt c(s) \frac{ds'}{s'} \lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(s).
            \end{align*}
        using parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:inefficient-smooth}), (\ref{eq:F12-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}), and the slowly-varying property.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
By parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) for the linear heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}), it suffices to show the bound for $n = 0$. We write
        \begin{align*}
            \nabla F_{tx} (s)
                &=  e^{\frac12 s \Delta} \nabla F_{tx} (\tfrac12 s) \\
                &= e^{\frac12 s \Delta} \nabla \Bigl( \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \nabla F_{12} \Bigr)(\tfrac12 s) \\
                &= \nabla e^{\frac12 s \Delta} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, (\tfrac12 s) + e^{\frac12 s \Delta} \Bigl( {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi + \nabla^{(2)} F_{12} \Bigr) (\tfrac12 s),
        \end{align*}
    using the fact that the electric field satisfies the linear heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}) in the first line, the definition of the Amp\'ere tension field in the second line, and the product rule in the last line. We individually estimate each term in the last line. For the first term, 
        \[
            \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \nabla) e^{\frac12 s \Delta} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, (\tfrac12 s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                \lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(\tfrac12 s). 
        \]
    by parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) and the Amp\'ere tension field bound (\ref{eq:amp-env}). For the second term,
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 e^{\frac12 s \Delta} ({\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi)(\tfrac12 s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| (s^\frac12\nabla) ({\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi) (\tfrac12 s)\bigr\|_{L^1_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \mathtt c(\tfrac12 s),
        \end{align*}
    by Sobolev embedding, Cauchy-Schwarz, and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}). For the third and last terms,  
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 e^{\frac12 s \Delta} (\phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi)(\tfrac12 s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| s^\frac12 e^{\frac12 s \Delta} (\nabla^{(2)} F_{12})(\tfrac12 s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \Bigr)\cdot \mathtt c(\tfrac12 s). 
        \end{align*}
    using the magnetic field bound (\ref{eq:F12-env}). Collecting the previous calculations and appealing to the slowly-varying property, $\mathtt c(s) \sim \mathtt c(\tfrac12 s)$, we conclude the desired bound.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
We claim that the right-hand side of the covariant heat equation for the Schr\"odinger tension field obeys the bound
        \begin{align}\label{eq:css-rhs}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl( \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}   + \underline s^{-1} \bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s).
        \end{align}
    Assuming the claim, we can prove the desired bound by applying parabolic smoothing. Indeed, in the case $n = 0$, the maximum principle (\ref{eq:maximum-principle}) and Duhamel's formula applied to (\ref{eq:CSS-heat}) yield
        \begin{align*}
            \| s^{-\frac12} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\, (s) \|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s} \Bigr)^\frac12 \bigl\| {s'}^\frac12 \cdot \bigl(\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}\bigr) (s') \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \, \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s} \Bigr)^\frac12 \cdot \Bigl( \| \phi(s') \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \underline s^{-1} \Bigr)  \cdot \mathtt c(s') \, \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                &\lesssim \int_0^s  \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s} \Bigr)^{\frac12 - \frac1{1000}} \cdot \Bigl( \| \phi(s) \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  +  \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{s}{s'}\Bigr) \cdot \underline s^{-1} + \underline s^{-1} \Bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s) \, \frac{ds'}{s'}\\
                &\lesssim \Bigl(  \| \phi (s) \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \underline s^{-1}  \Bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s),
        \end{align*}
    using the Brezis-Gallou\"et-type inequality (\ref{eq:brezis-0}) and the slowly-varying property. For higher-derivatives, we apply the abstract dyadic smoothing (\ref{eq:dyadic-smooth}) to the equation (\ref{eq:CSS-heat}) for the Schr\"odinger tension field, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^{-\frac12} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\, (s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| s^{-\frac12} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\,(s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| {s'}^\frac12 \cdot ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} \bigl(\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}\bigr) (s')\bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s'} L^2_x ([\frac12 s, s])} \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \underline s^{-1} \Bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s)
        \end{align*}
    as desired. 

    It remains to establish the claim. We compute via the product rule
         \begin{align*}
            (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)}\bigl(\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}\bigr)
                &= \sum_{a + b + c = n} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(c)} \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)} {\bf D} \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} {\bf D} \phi \\
                    &\qquad +  \sum_{a + b = n}  (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} \mathsf Q \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} {\bf D} \phi,
         \end{align*}
    abbreviating the electromagnetic field terms by $\mathsf Q \in \{ \nabla F_{12}, F_{tx}\}$. The best terms are the ``balanced'' ones, where derivatives are evenly distributed, 
         \[
            (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(c)} \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)} {\bf D} \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} {\bf D} \phi,
         \]
    for $a + b + c = n$ with $c \neq 0$. Placing the first factor in $L^\infty$ and estimating the remaining two factors in $L^2$ via Lemma \ref{lem:bilinear}, we arrive at 
         \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 (-) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(c)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| s^{-\frac12} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} (s {\bf D}^{(2)}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 \cdot \mathtt c(s),
         \end{align*}
    using parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) for the first two factors and the envelope estimate for higher-derivatives of the Hessian (\ref{eq:no-loss}) for the last factor. The remaining terms are ``unbalanced'', i.e. we will always see at least one undifferentiated factor of $\phi$, 
         \[
            \phi \cdot  (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)} {\bf D} \phi \cdot  (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} {\bf D} \phi,  \qquad (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} \mathsf Q \cdot  (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} {\bf D} \phi,
         \]
    for $a + b = n$. Estimating $\phi$ in $L^\infty$ and the remaining factors in $L^2$ via Lemma \ref{lem:bilinear}, 
         \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 ( - ) \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \Bigl( \|\phi \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \| (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} \mathsf Q \|_{L^2_x}\Bigr) \bigl\| s^{-\frac12} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} (s {\bf D}^{(2)}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                    &\qquad + \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b)} {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a + 1)} \mathsf Q  \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \underline s^{-1} \Bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s),
         \end{align*}
    using the envelope bounds for the derivatives of the covariant Hessian (\ref{eq:no-loss}) and the electromagnetic field (\ref{eq:F12-env}), (\ref{eq:Ftx-env}) for the ``high-frequency'' factors, and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) and the electromagnetic field bounds (\ref{eq:nabla-F12-Lp}), (\ref{eq:Fmunu-Lp}) for the ``low-frequency'' factors. This completes the proof of the claim and thereby the proposition.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:tension-diff}
    Let $(A, \phi)$, $(A', \phi')$ be smooth solutions on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ to the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}) in caloric-temporal gauge (\ref{eq:CTC}). Then for any $0 < s_* < \tfrac1{1000} \underline s$, and each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$, we have:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Amp\'ere tension field difference bound, higher-order terms).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Amp-diff}
            \begin{split}
                \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}s} L^2_x}
                    &\lesssim_{\underline s} \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot  \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 + \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr)  .
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Amp\'ere tension field difference bound, lower-order terms).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Amp-diff-lot}
            \begin{split}
                \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} + \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}s} L^2_x}
                    &\lesssim_{\underline s} \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0}.
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Electric field $L^2_{ds/s} L^2_x$-difference bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ftx-diff}
                \bigl\| s^\frac12 (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(n)} \delta F_{tx} \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                    \lesssim_{\underline s, n} \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot\Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 + \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr) .
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Electric field difference bound at $s = \underline s$)}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ftx-diff-low}
                \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \delta \underline F_{tx} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                    \lesssim_{\underline s, n}\log^\frac12\Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 + \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr).
            \end{equation}
        
        
        \item \textup{(Schr\"odinger tension field difference bound).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:CSS-diff}
            \begin{split}
                \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s} L^2_x} &+ \bigl\|\delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)}\,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\,  \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}\\
                    &\lesssim_{\underline s} \Bigl(1 + \bigl\| \overline A_x \bigr\|_{L^4_x}\Bigr) \cdot \log^\frac12 \Bigl(\frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 + \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr). 
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
Applying the weighted energy estimate (\ref{eq:abs-heat-weight}) with $\gamma = \tfrac12$ to the heat equation (\ref{eq:amp-heat-1}) for $\delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\,$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \bigl\| s^{1 + \frac12} \delta ({\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi}\bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 1)} (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} , 
        \end{align*}
    using Cauchy-Schwarz and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}) to estimate the right-hand side. Thus, it remains to estimate the difference $s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\,$ in $L^2_{ds/s} L^2_x$. We argue by interpolating between decay of high-frequencies and summability of low-frequencies -- a l\'a Lemma \ref{lem:low-high-inter}, it suffices to show  
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, (s)\bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} s^\frac12 ,\\
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_*, \underline s])}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s}\log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 + \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0}\Bigr).
        \end{align*}
    The former is an immediate consequence of the envelope bound (\ref{eq:amp-env}). For the latter, we write the difference using Duhamel's formula and divide the analysis between two cases, 
        \begin{align*}
            s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, (s)
                &= s^\frac12 \Bigl( \int_0^{\frac12 s_*} + \int_{\frac12 s_*}^s \Bigr) e^{(s - s') \Delta} \delta ({\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi) (s') \,ds'\\
                &=: \mathrm{I} + \mathrm{II}. 
        \end{align*}
    
        The first term on the right is a $\text{high}\times\text{high} \to \text{low}$-type term -- more precisely, the regime $s' < \tfrac12 s_* < \tfrac12 s$. We leverage parabolic smoothing in $s$, writing $e^{(s - s') \Delta} = e^{\frac12 s \Delta} e^{(\frac12 s - s') \Delta}$, and decay of high-frequencies, 
        \begin{align*}
            \|\mathrm{I} \|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \int_0^{\frac12 s_*} \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^1_x} \, ds' \\
                &\lesssim \int_0^{\frac12 s_*} |s'|^\frac12 \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D}) {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 \cdot |s_*|^\frac12, 
        \end{align*}
    using the smoothing estimate (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) in the first line, Cauchy-Schwarz in the second, and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) in the third. Putting this in $L^2_{ds/s} ([s_*, \underline s])$, we see another factor of $\log^{1/2} (\underline s/s_*)$, which is acceptable. 
    
    The second term on the right is a $\text{medium}\times\text{medium} \to \text{low}$-type term, where both $s$ and $s'$ reside in the regime $[s_*, \underline s]$. Here we argue by almost-orthogonality, 
        \begin{align*}
            \| \mathrm{II} \|_{L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \int_{\frac12 s_*}^s s^\frac12  \bigl\| e^{(s - s') \Delta} ({\bf D} \phi \cdot \delta {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi + \delta {\bf D} \phi \cdot {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi)\bigr\|_{L^2_x} ds' \, \\
                &\lesssim \int_{\frac12 s_*}^s \Bigl( \frac{s}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac12 \Bigl( \bigl\|  {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \delta ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(2)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \bigl\| \delta ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D}) {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \Bigr) \frac{ds'}{s'}\\
                &\lesssim \int_{\frac12 s_*}^s \Bigl( \frac{s}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac12 \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \delta ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 1)} (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \frac{ds'}{s'} ,
        \end{align*}
    using smoothing in $(s - s')$ and Cauchy-Schwarz in the second line, and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}) of ${\bf D} \phi$ in the third. Viewing this as an integral operator acting on functions on $[\frac12 s_*, \underline s]$, we estimate the kernel, 
        \begin{align*}
            \sup_{s \in [s_*, \underline s]} \int_{\frac12 s_*}^s \Bigl( \frac{s}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac12 \frac{ds'}{s'}
                &= \sup_{s \in [s_*, \underline s]} \int_{s_*/2s}^1 \Bigl( \frac{1}{1 - s"} \Bigr)^\frac12 \frac{ds"}{s"} \sim \log \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr),\\
            \sup_{s' \in [\frac12 s_*, \underline s]} \int_{s'}^{\underline s} \Bigl( \frac{s}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac12 \frac{ds}{s} 
                &=\sup_{s' \in [\frac12 s_*, \underline s]} \int_{1}^{\underline s/s'} \Bigl( \frac{1}{1 - s"}\Bigr)^\frac12 \frac{ds"}{s"} \lesssim 1.
         \end{align*}
    Thus, by Schur's test, 
         \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-i}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_*, \underline s])} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \cdot \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \bigl\| \delta(s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 1)} (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}.
         \end{align*}
    Collecting the previous inequalities, we conclude the desired bound.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
It suffices to show the stronger bound
        \[
            \bigl\| s^{\frac14} \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x}
                \lesssim_{\underline s} \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0}.
        \]
Writing this term using Duhamel's formula for (\ref{eq:amp-heat-2}) and then applying parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}), 
        \begin{align*}
             \bigl\| \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \int_0^s \bigl\| \delta (\phi \cdot F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi) (s') \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \frac{ds'}{s'} \\
                &\lesssim \int_0^s \Bigl( \frac{s'}{s - s'} \Bigr)^\frac14 \bigl\| \delta (\phi \cdot {s'}^\frac14 F_{12} \cdot ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi) (s')\bigr\|_{L^{4/3}_x} \, \frac{ds'}{s'}.
        \end{align*}
We divide into three cases depending on where the difference operator falls, and then estimating the remaining factors by parabolic smoothing for the magnetic field (\ref{eq:F12-sobolev}), ${\bf D} \phi$ (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}), and $\phi$. When the difference falls on $\phi$, we estimate it by (\ref{eq:phi-diff}), 
        (\ref{eq:phi-diff})
        \begin{align*}
            |s'|^\frac34 \cdot \bigl\| \delta \phi \cdot F_{12} \cdot {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{4/3}}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \delta \phi \bigr\|_{L^2 + L^\infty} \bigl\| {s'}^\frac14 F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^4}  \bigl\| ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty \cap L^2}\\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \Bigl( 1 + \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s'} \Bigr) \Bigr)  \cdot \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0}. 
        \end{align*}
When the difference falls on the magnetic field, we estimate it by (\ref{eq:F12-diff-lot}),
        \begin{align*}
            |s'|^\frac34 \cdot \bigl\| \phi \cdot  \delta F_{12} \cdot {\bf D}\phi \bigr\|_{L^{4/3}}
                &\lesssim |s'|^\frac14 \bigl\| {s'}^\frac18 \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty} \bigl\| {s'}^\frac18 \delta F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2}  \bigl\| {s'}^\frac14 {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^4}\\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} |s'|^{\frac14} \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0}. 
        \end{align*}
When the difference falls on ${\bf D} \phi$, we simply write 
         \begin{align*}
            |s'|^\frac34 \cdot \bigl\| \phi \cdot  F_{12} \cdot \delta {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{4/3}}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty} \bigl\| {s'}^\frac14 F_{12} \bigr\|_{L^4}  \bigl\| \delta ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2}\\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \Bigl( 1 + \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s'} \Bigr) \Bigr)  \cdot \bigl\| \delta ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2},
        \end{align*}
and then take Cauchy-Schwarz in $ds'/s'$ to see the $\mathpzc{E}^0$-metric. Altogether, these calculations yield a bound of the form 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \delta \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp-ii}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \Bigl(1 + \log \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s} \Bigr)\Bigr) \cdot \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}_0}.
        \end{align*}
Multiplying by $s^{1/4}$ handles the logarithmic divergence near $s = 0$. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
By parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) for the linear heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}), it suffices to consider $n = 0$. Interpolating via Lemma \ref{lem:low-high-inter}, the desired bound follows provided we show decay of high-frequencies $s \leq s_*$ and summability of low-frequencies $s \geq s_*$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 F_{tx} (s)\bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} s^\frac12 \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{\, s\,} \Bigr) ,\\
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 F_{tx} \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x([s_*, \underline s])}
                &\lesssim \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} +  |s_*|^\frac12  \Bigr). 
        \end{align*}
    The high frequency decay follows as an immediate consequence of the electric field bound (\ref{eq:Fmunu-Lp}) and the Brezis-Gallou\"et-type inequality (\ref{eq:brezis}). For the latter, we recall the definition of the Amp\'ere tension field 
        \begin{align*}
            s^\frac12 \delta F_{tx} 
                = s^\frac12 \delta \Bigl( \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \nabla F_{12}\Bigr) .
        \end{align*}
    The Amp\'ere tension field difference was controlled in (\ref{eq:Amp-diff})-(\ref{eq:Amp-diff-lot}), while the magnetic field difference was controlled in (\ref{eq:F12-diff}). For the contribution of $\delta \cdot (\phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi)$, we write 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| s^\frac12 \delta (\phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi)\bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x([s_*, \underline s])}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{s, x} ([s_*, \underline s])} \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \bigl\| \delta \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s (L^2 + L^\infty)_x ([s_*, \underline s])} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} (L^\infty \cap L^2)_x} \\
                &\lesssim \log^{\frac12} \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 1)} (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} + \bigl\| \delta \underline \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x},
        \end{align*}
    by the Brezis-Gallou\"et-type bound (\ref{eq:brezis}), its difference analogue (\ref{eq:phi-diff}), and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}). Collecting the previous bounds completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
By parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:standard-heat}) for the linear heat equation (\ref{eq:Fmunu-heat}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \delta \underline F_{tx} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim_n \bigl\| \delta\underline F_{tx} (\tfrac12 \underline s)\bigr\|_{L^2_x}. 
        \end{align*}
    Expanding via the definition of the Amp\'ere tension field,
        \begin{align*}
             \delta F_{tx} (\tfrac12 \underline s)
                =  \delta \Bigl( \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc amp}}}\, + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi + \nabla F_{12}\Bigr) (\tfrac12 \underline s). 
        \end{align*}
    The difference of the Amp\'ere tension field was estimated in (\ref{eq:Amp-diff})-(\ref{eq:Amp-diff-lot}), while the difference of the magnetic field as estimated in (\ref{eq:F12-diff}). When the difference falls on $\phi$, we use (\ref{eq:phi-diff}) and parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}). When the difference falls on ${\bf D} \phi$, we use (\ref{eq:Dphi-s-diff-2}) and estimate $\phi$ by (\ref{eq:brezis-0}). Since we are working on the dyadic scale $[\underline s/2, \underline s]$, the ensuing extra negative powers of $s$ and logarithmic factors are harmless.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
By the envelope bound for the Schr\"odinger tension field (\ref{eq:css-env}) and the Brezis-Gallou\"et-type bound (\ref{eq:brezis}),  
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\, (s) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s, \|} s^{\frac12} \cdot \Bigl( \| \phi(t, s) \|_{L^\infty_x} \bigl\| \overline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \underline s^{-1} \Bigr) \cdot \mathtt c(s) \\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} 1 .
        \end{align*}
    Thus, applying the abstract difference bound from Lemma \ref{lem:diff-smooth} to the equation for the Schr\"odinger tension field (\ref{eq:CSS-heat}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s L^2_x} &+ \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc sch}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \bigl\| \delta \overline A_x \bigr\|_{L^4_x} + \bigl\| \nabla \delta  \overline A_x  \bigr\|_{L^2_x}  + \bigl\| \overline A_x \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \bigl\| \delta \overline A_x \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \\
                    &\qquad+ \bigl\|s \cdot \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}\\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \Bigl(1 + \bigl\| \overline A_x \bigr\|_{L^4_x} \Bigr) \cdot \log^\frac12\Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 + \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr) \\
                    &\qquad+ \bigl\|s \cdot \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x},
        \end{align*}
    estimating the difference of the magnetic potential via (\ref{eq:F12-diff})\footnote{Actually, if one inspects the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:diff-smooth}, we can put more powers of $s$ on the magnetic field and estimate it using the lower-order estimate (\ref{eq:F12-diff-lot}). }and (\ref{eq:Ax-diff}). Thus, it remains to show
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\|s \cdot \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 +  \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr).
        \end{align*}
    To prove this estimate, we interpolate between high and low frequencies using Lemma \ref{lem:low-high-inter}, reducing the task to showing 
       \begin{align*}
            \bigl\|s \, (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})})\bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} s^\frac12 \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s} \Bigr),\\
            \bigl\|s \, \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})}) \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_*, \underline s])}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 +  \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr).
       \end{align*} 
    
    
    For the high-frequency bound, recall that, during the proof of the envelope bound (\ref{eq:css-env}), we showed that 
       \begin{align*}
            \bigl\|s \, (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq 2027)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})})\bigr\|_{L^2_x}
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} s^\frac12 \Bigl( 1 +  \| \phi(s) \|_{L^\infty_x} \Bigr).
       \end{align*}
    Thus the high-frequency bound for $s \leq s_*$ follows from the Brezis-Gallou\"et-type inequality (\ref{eq:brezis}). 
    
    For the low-frequency bound, we compute 
       \begin{align*}
            s \cdot \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(n)} (\text{R.H.S.(\ref{eq:CSS-heat})})
                &= \sum_{a + b = n} \delta \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a + 1)} \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi \\
                &\qquad +  \sum_{a + b + c = n} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(c)} \phi \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a + 1)} \phi \cdot \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi \\
                    &\qquad + \sum_{a + b = n} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} \delta s^\frac12 \mathsf Q \cdot (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi  \\
                    &\qquad + \sum_{a + b = n} (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)}  s^\frac12 \mathsf Q \cdot \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi \\
                &=: \mathrm{I}_n + \mathrm{II}_n + \mathrm{III}_n + \mathrm{IV}_n,
       \end{align*}
    where $\mathsf Q \in \{ \nabla F_{12}, F_{tx}\}$. For the first term, we estimate the difference of the scalar field in $L^2 + L^\infty$ via (\ref{eq:phi-diff}), and the remaining terms in $L^2_{ds/s} (L^\infty \cap L^2)_x$ and $L^2_{ds/s} L^\infty_x$ via parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}), 
       \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \mathrm{I}_n \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_*, \underline s])}
                &\lesssim \sum_{a + b = n}\bigl\| \delta \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s (L^2 + L^\infty)_x ([s_*, \underline s])} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} (L^\infty \cap L^2)_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^\infty_x} \\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\| \delta \underline \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(2)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \Bigr) ,
       \end{align*}
    which is acceptable. For the second term, we make analogous moves,
       \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \mathrm{II}_n \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_*, \underline s])}
                &\lesssim \sum_{a + b + c = n} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a)}\phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_s (L^2 + L^\infty)_x ([s_*, \underline s])} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(a + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} (L^\infty \cap L^2)_x} \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}  \\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \log^\frac12 \Bigl(\frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} (s^\frac12 {\bf D}) \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x}
       \end{align*}
    where we bound $a = 0$ via the Brezis-Gallou\"et-type inequality (\ref{eq:brezis}). For the third term, we estimate the electromagnetic field differences via (\ref{eq:F12-diff}) and (\ref{eq:Ftx-diff}) and ${\bf D} \phi$ via parabolic smoothing (\ref{eq:Dphi-sobolev}), (\ref{eq:Dphi-strichartz-heat}) 
       \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \mathrm{III}_n \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \sum_{a + b = n} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)} \delta s^\frac12 \mathsf Q \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^\infty_x}  \\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( |s_*|^\frac12 + \operatorname*{dist}_{\mathpzc{E}^0} \Bigr) .
       \end{align*}
    For the fourth term, we estimate the electromagnetic field via (\ref{eq:nabla-F12-Lp}) and (\ref{eq:Fmunu-Lp}), and the ensuing contribution of $\phi(s)$ via the Brezis-Gallou\"et-type inequality (\ref{eq:brezis}), 
       \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \mathrm{IV}_n \bigr\|_{L^1_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x ([s_*, \underline s])} 
                &\lesssim \sum_{a + b = n} \bigl\| (s^\frac12 \nabla)^{(a)}  s^\frac12 \mathsf Q \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^\infty_x ([s_*, \underline s])} \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(b + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim_{\underline s} \log^\frac12 \Bigl( \frac{\underline s}{s_*} \Bigr)\cdot  \bigl\| \delta (s^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(\leq n)} (s^\frac12 {\bf D})\phi \bigr\|_{L^2_{\frac{ds}{s}} L^2_x} .
       \end{align*}
    Taking $n \leq 2027$, these terms are all acceptable.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- numremark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:hihilo}
    The Amp\'ere tension field difference bound (\ref{eq:Amp-diff}) is analogous to the electric potential difference bound \cite[Lemma 5.3]{Lim2018} in the setting of the Jackiw-Pi Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:JP-CSS}) in Coulomb gauge. Unfortunately, in our setting, there seems to be an extra logarithmic divergence arising from the term 
        \[
            (\partial_s - \Delta)^{-1} ({\bf D} \phi \cdot \delta {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi).
        \]
    One can view this as a $\text{high}\times \text{high} \to \text{low}$ paraproduct. If we try to estimate this in a very weak norm, e.g. $L^1$, we obtain by Cauchy-Schwarz
        \[
            \bigl\| (\partial_s - \Delta)^{-1} ({\bf D} \phi \cdot \delta {\bf D}^{(2)} \phi) \bigr\|_{L^1_x}
                \leq \int_0^s \bigl\| {\bf D} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \bigl\| \delta ({s'}^\frac12 {\bf D})^{(2)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \frac{ds'}{s'}
        \]
    The difference is $L^2_{ds/s}$-summable, however the factor of ${\bf D} \phi$ is merely $L^\infty_s$. Furthermore, there does not seem to be any room to leverage Strichartz estimates, as all the powers of $s'$ have been ``used up".
<!-- end numremark-1 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
Our choice of caloric-temporal gauge takes inspiration from the work of Oh \cite{Oh2014a, Oh2015a} on the hyperbolic Yang-Mills equation on $\mathbb R^{1 + 3}$, along with its later use by Gavrus \cite{Gavrus2022}. Indeed, similar to these works, our setting is ``sub-critical'' in some sense, so the gauge-choice implicitly distinguishes a particular choice of ``low-frequency'', $s = \underline s$ in our notation.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
We say that $\chi : [0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s] \to \mathbb R$ is \textit{regular gauge-transformation} if it has the following regularity properties: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\nabla_{t, x, s} \chi \in C^\infty_{t, s} H^\infty_x ([0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s])$.
        
        \item $\chi \in C^\infty_{t, x,s, \mathrm{loc}} ([0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s])$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:ctc-exists}
    Let $(\widetilde A, \widetilde \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ solving the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}). Then 
        \begin{align*}
            A_{\bf a} 
                &:= \widetilde A_{\bf a} + \partial_{\bf a} \chi, \\
            \phi 
                &:= e^{i \chi} \widetilde\phi ,
        \end{align*}
    where 
         \[
            \chi 
                := -(\partial_s)^{-1} A_s - (\partial_t)^{-1} \underline A_t - \Delta^{-1} \partial^\ell {\underline {A}_\ell}_{|t = 0} ,
        \]
    solves (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}) in caloric-temporal gauge (\ref{eq:CTC}) with initial data in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-sbar}). Moreover, if $(\widetilde A, \widetilde \phi)$ is a smooth solution, then $\chi$ is a regular gauge transformation, and thereby $(A, \phi)$ is also a smooth solution.
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proposition-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:A-ctc}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ to the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}) in caloric-temporal gauge (\ref{eq:CTC}) with initial data in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-sbar}). Then the electric potential obeys:  
    \begin{itemize}
        \item transport equation in $s$,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:At-transport}
            \begin{split}
                \partial_s A_t 
                    &= \nabla F_{tx},\\
                {A_t}_{|s = \underline s}
                    &= 0,
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
    curl-free part of the magnetic potential obeys:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item transport equation in $s$,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ax-transport-cf}
            \begin{split}
                \partial_s \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A_x 
                    &= 0,\\
                {\mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A_x}_{|s = \underline s}
                    &= \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} \underline A_x, 
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}

        \item transport equation in $t$ at $s = \underline s$, 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ax-transport-t}
            \begin{split}
                \partial_t \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} \underline A_x 
                    &= \underline F_{tx},\\
                \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} {\underline A_x}_{|t = 0}
                    &= 0.
            \end{split}
            \end{equation} 
    \end{itemize}
    and the divergence-free part of the magnetic potential obeys: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item transport equation in $s$,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ax-transport-df}
            \begin{split}
                \partial_s \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A_x 
                    &= \nabla F_{12},\\
                {\mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A_x}_{|s = \underline s}
                    &= \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} \underline A_x,
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}
        
        \item modified Biot-Savart law at $s = \underline s$, 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ax-elliptic}
                \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} \underline A_x
                    = \nabla^{-1} \Bigl(  (1 - |\underline\phi|^2) \cdot \underline F_{12} +\underline{{\bf D} \phi} \cdot \underline{{\bf D} \phi} \Bigr) + \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} \bigl( \underline \phi \cdot \underline{{\bf D} \phi} \bigr).
            \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-21 -->
<!-- proposition-22: body_md -->
\label{thm:ctc-bounds}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a smooth solution on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \times [0, \underline s]$ to the paradifferential formulation of the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:dP-CSS}) in caloric-temporal gauge (\ref{eq:CTC}) with initial data in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-sbar}). Then the following hold:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textup{(Bounds for curl-free part of magnetic potential).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ax-ctc-cf}
                \bigl\| \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A_x \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, s} H^{100}_x} 
                    \lesssim_{\underline s} T.
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Bounds for divergence-free part of magnetic potential).} 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ax-ctc-df}
                \bigl\| \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A_x \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, s} L^4_x} + \bigl\| \nabla \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A_x \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, s} H^{1/2}_x}
                    \lesssim_{\underline s} 1.
            \end{equation}

        \item \textup{(Uniform bounds for magnetic potential).}
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:Ax-ctc}
