        \end{align*}
    estimating the difference in $L^4_{t, x}$ using Strichartz (\ref{eq:covar-str-global}), and the difference in $L^\infty_t L^2_x$ using (\ref{eq:heat-lip}).
<!-- end proof-93 -->
<!-- remark-23: body_md -->
One can probably show that the gauge-transformation is in fact Lipschitz continuous by refining our crude interpolation argument with Strichartz-type bounds for the differences.
<!-- end remark-23 -->
<!-- remark-24: body_md -->
It is not difficult to show that $\chi \in L^\infty_t H^{5/2-}_x ([0, T] \times \mathbb R^2)$, so in fact the magnetic potential in DeTurck gauge has regularity $\nabla A_x \in L^\infty_t H^{1/2 -} ([0, T] \times \mathbb R^2)$.
<!-- end remark-24 -->
<!-- proposition-30: body_md -->
\label{prop:CSS-Gauss}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ obeying the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}). Then the magnetic field and charge density obey the density-flux identities,
        \begin{align}\label{eq:density-flux1}
             \partial_t F_{12} 
                &= \partial^j \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi),\\
            \partial_t \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2)
                &= \partial^j \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi).\label{eq:density-flux2}
        \end{align}
    In particular, the Gauss tension field obeys the transport equation
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:t-gauss}
            \partial_t \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, = 0. 
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-30 -->
<!-- proof-94: body_md -->
From the Bianchi identity (\ref{eq:bianchi}) and Ampere's law from (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}), we compute the density-flux identity (\ref{eq:density-flux1}) for the curvature,
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_t F_{12} 
                &= \partial_1 F_{t2} - \partial_2 F_{t1} \\
                &= \partial_1 \left( \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_1 \phi) - \partial_2 F_{12} \right) - \partial_2 \left( - \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_2 \phi) - \partial_1 F_{12} \right)\\
                &= \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \phi) = \partial^j \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi).
        \end{align*}
    Using the covariant Schr\"odinger equation from (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}), we compute the density-flux identity (\ref{eq:density-flux2}) for the charge, 
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_t \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2)
                &= - \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_t \phi) \\
                &= \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j \phi) = \partial^j \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi).
        \end{align*}
    Subtracting the two equations, we conclude that the Gauss tension field satisfies (\ref{eq:t-gauss}).
<!-- end proof-94 -->
<!-- proposition-31: body_md -->
\label{prop:conserve}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ satisfying the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}). Then 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:energy-density-flux}
            \tfrac12 \partial_t \Bigl( \overline{{\bf D}^j \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi + |F_{12}|^2 + \tfrac\lambda4 (1 -|\phi|^2)^2 \Bigr)
                = \partial^j \operatorname{Re}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi) - \varepsilon\indices{_j^k} \partial_k (F\indices{_t^j} F_{12}).
        \end{equation}
    Furthermore, if $(A, \phi)$ is a smooth solution, then the abelian Higgs energy is conserved under the flow, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:energy-conservation}
            \mathcal E_{\mathrm{AH}} [A(t), \phi(t)] = \mathcal E_{\mathrm{AH}} [A(0), \phi(0)] , \qquad \text{for all $t \in [0, T]$}.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-31 -->
<!-- proof-95: body_md -->
Working in a gauge-covariant fashion, we multiply the covariant Schr\"odinger equation by ${\bf D}_t \phi$,
	\begin{align*}
		0 
			&= \operatorname{Re} \Bigl(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} (i {\bf D}_t \phi + {\bf D}^j {\bf D}_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \phi)\Bigr)\\
			&= \partial^j \operatorname{Re}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi) - \operatorname{Re}(\overline{{\bf D}^j {\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi) - \partial_t \tfrac12 \tfrac\lambda4 (1 - |\phi|^2)^2 \\
            &= \partial^j \operatorname{Re}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi) - \operatorname{Re}(\overline{{\bf D}_t {\bf D}^j \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi) - F\indices{_t^j} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) - \partial_t \tfrac12 \tfrac\lambda4 (1 - |\phi|^2)^2 \\
            &= \partial^j \operatorname{Re}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi) - F\indices{_t^j} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) - \tfrac12 \partial_t \Bigl( \overline{{\bf D}^j \phi} {\bf D}_j \phi - \tfrac\lambda4 (1 - |\phi|^2)^2 \Bigr),
	\end{align*}
differentiating-by-parts and commuting covariant derivatives appropriately, and similarly multiplying Ampere's law by $F_{tj}$ appropriately, 
    \begin{align*}
        0 
            &= F\indices{_t^j} \Bigl( \varepsilon\indices{_j^k} F_{tk} - \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) + \varepsilon\indices{_j^k} \partial_k F_{12} \Bigr) \\
            &= - F\indices{_t^j} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) + \varepsilon\indices{_j^k} \partial_k (F\indices{_t^j} F_{12}) - \varepsilon\indices{_j^k} \partial_k F\indices{_t^j} F_{12} \\
            &= - F\indices{_t^j} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) + \varepsilon\indices{_j^k} \partial_k (F\indices{_t^j} F_{12}) + \partial_t F_{12} \, F_{12}\\
            &= - F\indices{_t^j} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) + \varepsilon\indices{_j^k} \partial_k (F\indices{_t^j} F_{12}) + \tfrac12 \partial_t \bigl(|F_{12}|^2 \bigr),
    \end{align*}
differentiating-by-parts in the second line and using the Bianchi identity (\ref{eq:bianchi}) in the third line. Subtracting the previous two calculations, we obtain the density-flux relation (\ref{eq:energy-density-flux}). 

To prove the conservation of the abelian Higgs energy (\ref{eq:energy-conservation}), fix a smooth cut-off $\chi \in C^\infty_c (\mathbb R^2)$ such that $\chi \equiv 1$ in a neighborhood of the origin, and test the identity (\ref{eq:energy-density-flux}) against its rescaling $\chi(\tfrac{x}{R})$ for $R > 0$. Integrating-by-parts on $[0, t] \times \mathbb R^2$ gives the schematic identity
    \begin{align*}
        \int_{\mathbb R^2} \mathfrak e[A(t'), \phi(t')] \, \chi\bigl( \tfrac{x}{R} \bigr) \ dx \Big|_{t = 0}^{t' = t}
            = \frac1R \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb R^2} (\nabla \chi)\bigl( \tfrac{x}{R} \bigr) \Bigl( {\bf D}_t \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi + F_{tx} \cdot F_{12} \Bigr) \, dx dt',
    \end{align*}
abbreviating $\mathfrak e[A(t), \phi (t)]$ for the energy density. Taking $R \to \infty$, the expression on the left converges to the differences of the energies by the dominated convergence theorem, 
    \[
        \lim_{R \to \infty} \text{L.H.S.} = \mathcal E_{\text{AH}}[A(t), \phi(t)] - \mathcal E_{\text{AH}}[A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}].
    \]
On the right-hand side, an application of Cauchy-Schwarz and passing to the limit yields 
    \[
        \Big| \text{R.H.S.} \Big|
            \lesssim_t \frac{1}R \sup_{t' \in [0, t]}\Big( \| {\bf D}_t \phi \|_{L^2_x} \| {\bf D} \phi\|_{L^2_x} + \| F_{tx}\|_{L^2} \| F_{12} \|_{L^2_x}  \Big) \overset{R \to \infty}{\longrightarrow} 0.
    \]
Indeed, it is easy to check that the supremum is $O_t (1)$ for smooth solutions using the equation and Sobolev embedding (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}).
<!-- end proof-95 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:vorticity}
    Let $(A, \phi) \in \mathfrak E$ be a finite-energy configuration on $\mathbb R^2$. Then 
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item \textup{(Vorticity identity).} 
                \begin{equation}\label{eq:vorticity-identity}
                    \begin{split}
                        \omega(A, \phi)
                            &= (1 - |\phi|^2) F_{12} + 2 \operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}_1 \phi} {\bf D}_2 \phi).
                    \end{split}
                    \end{equation}

            \item \textup{(Modified Biot-Savart law).} 
                \begin{align}
                    \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A 
                        &= \nabla^{-1} \omega(A, \phi) + \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} (\phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi ) .\label{eq:BS-low}
                \end{align}
        \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-96: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Differentiating and commuting appropriately yields
        \begin{align*}
            \omega(A, \phi)
                &= F_{12} + \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi) \\
                &= F_{12} + \varepsilon_{jk} \left( \operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}^j \phi} {\bf D}^k \phi) + \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^j {\bf D}^k  \phi) \right) \\
                &= (1 - |\phi|^2) F_{12} + 2 \operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}_1 \phi} {\bf D}_2 \phi),
        \end{align*}
    as desired.

        \item We write 
                \[
                    \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A 
                        = \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} (A + \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D} \phi)) - \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D} \phi),
                \]
            and use the Biot-Savart law to re-express the first term on the right-hand side. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-96 -->
<!-- proposition-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:vorticity-II}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$. Then the vorticity obeys the density-flux identity
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:difference-flux}
            \partial_t \omega(A, \phi)
                    = \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j \Bigl( (1 - |\phi|^2) F\indices{_t^k}  +  2 \operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}^k \phi)\Bigr).
        \end{equation} 
     Furthermore, if $(A, \phi)$ is a smooth solution to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation, then the topological degree is conserved under the flow, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:top-conserve}
            \deg[A(t_1), \phi(t_1)] = \deg[A(t_2), \phi(t_2)] \qquad \text{for all $t_1, t_2 \in [0, T]$}.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-32 -->
<!-- proof-97: body_md -->
By the Bianchi identity (\ref{eq:bianchi}),
            \begin{align*}
                \partial_t \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j A 
                    = \partial_t F_{12} 
                    = \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j F\indices{_t^k} .
            \end{align*}
        Differentiating the charge current with respect to $h$ and commuting appropriately gives
            \begin{align*}
                \partial_t \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi) 
                    &= \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j \Big( \operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}^k \phi) + \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_t {\bf D}^k \phi) \Big)\\
                    &= \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j \Big( \operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}^k \phi) + \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k {\bf D}_t \phi) - |\phi|^2 F\indices{_t^k} \Big)\\
                    &= \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j \Big( 2\operatorname{Im}(\overline{{\bf D}_t \phi} {\bf D}^k \phi)  - |\phi|^2 F\indices{_t^k} \Big).
            \end{align*}
        Collecting the two calculations yields (\ref{eq:difference-flux}). 

        The proof of conservation of the topological degree (\ref{eq:top-conserve}) is similar to that of conservation of the abelian Higgs energy -- simply integrate the density-flux relation (\ref{eq:difference-flux}) appropriately.
<!-- end proof-97 -->
<!-- remark-25: body_md -->
The density-flux relation for the vorticity (\ref{eq:difference-flux}) is completely algebraic and holds for any configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$. Moreover, the conservation of the topological degree (\ref{eq:top-conserve}) holds as long as $(A, \phi)$ has uniformly bounded abelian Higgs energy and finite $L^2$-length, i.e. 
    \[
        \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \mathcal E_{\textup{AH}} [A(t), \phi(t)] + \int_0^T \| {\bf D}_t \phi  \|_{L^2_x} + \| F_{tx} \|_{L^2_x} \, dt < \infty.
    \]
    One can think of this as the statement that two configurations $(A(0), \phi(0))$ and $(A(T), \phi(T))$ have the same topological degree if they admit a ``reasonable'' homotopy.
<!-- end remark-25 -->
<!-- proposition-33: body_md -->
\label{prop:example}
    $(A^{(n, \alpha,\gamma)}, \phi^{(n, \alpha,\gamma)}) \in \mathfrak E^\infty \cap C^\infty (\mathbb R^2)$ are smooth configurations.
<!-- end proposition-33 -->
<!-- proof-98: body_md -->
For brevity, we suppress the dependence on the parameters and write $(A, \phi) \equiv (A^{(n, \alpha,\gamma)}, \phi^{(n, \alpha,\gamma)})$. It is easy to see by inspection that $(A, \phi) \in C^\infty (\mathbb R^2)$, so it remains to verify $(A, \phi) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$. 
    
    Computing the magnetic gradient in polar coordinates, 
        \begin{align*}
            {\bf D}_r \phi 
                &= \partial_r \phi \\
                &= \Bigl( - \partial_r \rho + i \gamma (1 - \rho) \frac{\log^{\gamma - 1} (2 + r)}{2 + r} \Bigr) \exp\bigl( i \log^{\gamma}(2 + r) \bigr) \exp\bigl( i \bigl( n\theta + \alpha \sin (\theta)\bigr) \bigr),\\ 
            {\bf D}_\theta \phi 
                &= (\partial_\theta - i A_\theta) \phi \\
                &= i (1 - \rho) \Bigl( \partial_\theta (n \theta + \alpha \sin(\theta)) - (n + \alpha \cos (\theta))\Bigr)\exp\bigl( i \bigl( n\theta + \alpha \sin (\theta)\bigr) \bigr) = 0.
        \end{align*}
    Then, since $\rho$ is smooth, compactly supported, and $(2 + r)^{-1} \log^{\gamma - 1} \in L^2 (r dr)$ whenever $\gamma < \tfrac12$, we see that ${\bf D} \phi \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$. More generally, observe that for any combination of magnetic derivatives, the contributions of the angular derivatives ${\bf D}_\theta$ vanish, while consecutive applications of the radial derivatives ${\bf D}_r$ remain smooth and can only improve decay. Thus, ${\bf D}^{(n)} \phi \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$ for any positive integer $n \in \mathbb N$. 
    
    For the curvature and charge density, 
        \begin{align*}
            F_{r \theta} 
                &= \partial_r A_\theta \\
                &= - \partial_r \rho \cdot (n + \alpha \cos (\theta)), \\
            \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2) 
                &= \tfrac12(1 - |1 - \rho|^2) \\
                &= \rho - \tfrac12 \rho^2,
        \end{align*}
    so it is easy to see that $F_{12}, \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \in C^\infty_c (\mathbb R^2)$ by choice of $\rho$.
<!-- end proof-98 -->
<!-- proposition-34: body_md -->
$(A^{(n, 0,\gamma)}, \phi^{(n, 0,\gamma)})$ is in Coulomb gauge.
<!-- end proposition-34 -->
<!-- proof-99: body_md -->
We calculate the divergence of the magnetic potential in polar coordinates, 
        \[
            \partial^j A_j = \Bigl( \tfrac1r + \partial_r \Bigr) A_r + \frac{1}{r^2} \partial_\theta A_\theta = -\alpha (1 - \rho) \sin(\theta). 
        \]  
    Thus, $A$ is in Coulomb gauge if and only if $\alpha = 0$.
<!-- end proof-99 -->
<!-- proposition-35: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\gamma \neq \gamma'$, then for each $1 \leq p < \infty$ we have 
            \[
				\phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)} - \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma')} \not\in L^p (\mathbb R^2).
			\]
        In particular, $\mathfrak E_\phi \not\subseteq \mathring \phi + L^p (\mathbb R^2)$ for any function $\mathring \phi : \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb C$. 
        
        \item If $n \neq 0$, then
            \[
                \nabla \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)} \not\in L^2 (\mathbb R^2).
            \] 
        In particular, $\mathfrak E_\phi \not\subseteq \dot H^1 (\mathbb R^2)$. 
        
        \item If $\alpha \neq \alpha'$, then 
            \[
				\bigl(\nabla - i A^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}\bigr) \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)} \not\in L^2 (\mathbb R^2).
			\]
        In particular, $\mathfrak E_\phi \not\subseteq \dot H^1_{\mathring A} (\mathbb R^2)$ for any connection $1$-form $\mathring A : \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R^2$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-35 -->
<!-- proof-100: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item This is due to non-resonant phase oscillation. Indeed, we calculate, 
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl|\phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)} - \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma')}\bigr|
                    = |1 - \rho| \cdot \bigl|\exp(i\log^\gamma (2 + r)) - \exp(i\log^{\gamma'} (2 + r))\bigr|,
            \end{align*}
        so, unless $\gamma = \gamma'$, we can easily find infinitely many unit-length intervals where the amplitude of the difference is of size, say, at least $c > 0$. 

        \item We calculate 
            \[  
                |\partial_\theta \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)} |
                    = |1 - \rho| \cdot |n + \alpha \cos (\theta)|,
            \]
        If $n \neq 0$, the calculation above shows that the gradient obeys the pointwise bound 
            \[
                \bigl|\nabla \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}\bigr|
                    \gtrsim \tfrac1r 
            \]
        in the region where $|\cos(\theta)| \ll 1$ and $r \gg 1$, so it is not $L^2$-integrable. 

        \item We calculate
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl|(\partial_\theta - i A^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}_\theta) \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)} \bigr| 
                    &= |1 - \rho| \cdot \Bigl| \partial_\theta (n \theta   \alpha \sin (\theta)) - (n + \alpha' \cos (\theta)) \Bigr|\\
                    &= |1 - \rho| \cdot |\alpha - \alpha'| \cdot |\cos(\theta)|.
            \end{align*}
        If $\alpha \neq \alpha'$, the calculation above shows that the gradient obeys the pointwise bound 
            \[
                \bigl| (\nabla - i A^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}) \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)} \bigr| 
                    \gtrsim \tfrac1r, 
            \]
        in the region where $|\cos(\theta)| \ll 1$ and $r \gg 1$, so it is not $L^2$-integrable. 

        Suppose now, towards a contradiction, that we can find a fixed connection $1$-form $\mathring A$ such that $\mathring {\bf D} \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}, \mathring {\bf D} \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)} \in L^2(\mathbb R^2)$, where $\mathring {\bf D} = \nabla - i \mathring A$. However, we can write  
            \begin{align*}
                (\nabla - i A^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}) \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)}
                    &= \mathring {\bf D} \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)} + i \bigl(\mathring A - A^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}\bigr) \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)},\\
                    &= \mathring {\bf D} \phi^{(n, \alpha', \gamma)} + i \Bigl(   (\nabla - i A^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}) \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)} - \mathring {\bf D} \phi^{(n, \alpha, \gamma)}\Bigr)\exp \Bigl( i (\alpha' - \alpha) \sin(\theta) \Bigr).
            \end{align*}
        By the assumptions and Proposition \ref{prop:example}, the right-hand side is in $L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$, a contradiction. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-100 -->
<!-- proposition-36: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ be a smooth configuration on $\mathbb R^2$ in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}). Then $A \in C^\infty (\mathbb R^2)$, and, for each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:A-Cinfty}
            \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} A \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}
                \lesssim_{\| \frac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \|_{L^2}, \| F_{12} \|_{H^{n + 1}}, \| {\bf D}^{(\leq 1)}{\bf D} \phi \|_{L^2}} 1.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-36 -->
<!-- proof-101: body_md -->
For each positive integer $n \in \mathbb N$, it follows from Sobolev embedding and the Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}) that 
        \[
            \| \nabla^{(n - 1)} \nabla A \|_{L^\infty}
                \lesssim \| F_{12} \|_{H^{n + 1}}.
        \]
    This proves (\ref{eq:A-Cinfty}) at top-order. At bottom-order, we interpolate,
        \[
            \| A \|_{L^\infty_x}
                \lesssim \| A \|_{L^4} + \| F_{12} \|_{H^1}.
        \]
    To estimate $A$ in $L^4$, we use the modified Biot-Savart law (\ref{eq:BS-low}) to write $A = \nabla^{-1} \omega (A, \phi) + \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi$. For the contribution of the charge current, 
        \begin{align*}
            \| \phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^4} 
                &\lesssim \| \phi \|_{L^\infty} \| {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^4} \\
                &\lesssim 1 + \| \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \|_{L^2}^2 + \| {\bf D}^{(\leq 1)} {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^2}^2
        \end{align*}
    estimating $\phi$ by the $L^\infty$-bound (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}), and its derivative by interpolation (\ref{eq:GN-interpolation}). For the contribution of the vorticity, 
        \begin{align*}
            \| \nabla^{-1} \omega (A, \phi) \|_{L^4}
                &\lesssim \| \omega(A, \phi) \|_{L^{4/3}} \\
                &\lesssim \| {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^2} \| {\bf D}\phi \|_{L^4} + \| \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \|_{L^2} \| F_{12} \|_{L^4}\\
                &\lesssim  \| {\bf D}^{(\leq 1)} {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^2}^2 + \| \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \|_{L^2} \| F_{12} \|_{H^1}. 
        \end{align*}
    using Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev in the first line, H\"older's inequality applied to the identity (\ref{eq:vorticity-identity}) in the second, and Sobolev embedding in the last. Collecting the inequalities above, we conclude (\ref{eq:A-Cinfty}) at bottom-order. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-101 -->
<!-- proposition-37: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ be a smooth configuration on $\mathbb R^2$ in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}). Then $\phi \in C^\infty (\mathbb R^2)$, and, for each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$, 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:phi-Cinfty}
            \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}
                \lesssim_{\| {\bf D}^{(\leq n + 1)} {\bf D} \phi \|_{L^2}, \| \frac12(1 - |\phi|^2) \|_{L^2}, \| F_{12} \|_{H^{n}}} 1.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-37 -->
<!-- proof-102: body_md -->
The case $n = 0$ is a consequence of the Sobolev-type estimate (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}). From here, we proceed inductively, assuming the result holds up to $n$, and aiming to prove the estimate for $n + 1$. To facilitate the analysis, observe the following schematic formula, 
        \[
            \nabla^{(n + 1)} \phi 
                = {\bf D}^{(n + 1)} \phi + (\nabla^{(\leq n)} A)^{(\leq n)} \nabla^{(\leq n)} \phi,
        \]
    where $\nabla^{(\leq n)}$ denotes differentiation up to order $n$, and $u^{(\leq n)}$ denotes a product consisting of up to $n$-many terms. It is not difficult to see the formula holds by an inductive application of the definition of the covariant derivative ${\bf D} = \nabla - i A$ and the product rule. It follows from the formula that 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \nabla^{(n + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(\leq n)} A \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x}^{\leq n} \, \bigl\| \nabla^{(\leq n)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} \\
                &\lesssim_{\| {\bf D}^{(\leq n + 1)} {\bf D}\phi \|_{L^2}, \| \frac12(1 - |\phi|^2) \|_{L^2}, \| F_{12} \|_{H^{n + 1}}} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 1)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 3)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^{\frac12} + 1 \\
                &\lesssim_{\| {\bf D}^{(\leq n + 2)} {\bf D}\phi \|_{L^2}, \| \frac12(1 - |\phi|^2) \|_{L^2}, \| F_{12} \|_{H^{n + 1}}} 1,
        \end{align*}
    using Sobolev embedding (\ref{eq:GNinfty}), the $C^k$-estimates for the magnetic potential (\ref{eq:A-Cinfty}), and the inductive hypothesis. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-102 -->
<!-- proposition-38: body_md -->
\label{prop:magnetic-lip-1}
\leavevmode
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Let $\Phi, \Psi \in (L^4 + L^\infty) (\mathbb R^2)$ such that $\Phi - \Psi \in H^1 (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:charge-perturb}
            \bigl\| |\Phi|^2 - |\Psi|^2 \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                \lesssim \Bigl( \| \Phi \|_{L^4_x + L^\infty_x} + \| \Psi \|_{L^4_x + L^\infty_x} \Bigr) \bigl\| \Phi - \Psi \bigr\|_{H^1_x}.
            \end{equation}
            Furthermore, fixing $\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} \in (L^4 + L^\infty) (\mathbb R^2)$, perturbations by $u, v \in H^1 (\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:charge-perturb-2}
                \bigl\| |\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} + u|^2 - |\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} + v|^2 \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    \lesssim \Bigl( \| \mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} \|_{L^4_x + L^\infty_x} + \| u \|_{H^1_x} + \| v \|_{H^1_x} \Bigr) \| u - v \|_{H^1_x}.
            \end{equation} 

        \item Let $A, B \in H^1_\mathrm{loc} (\mathbb R^2)$ such that $\nabla (A - B) \in L^2 (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:field-perturb}
                \bigl\| (F_A)_{12} - (F_B)_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    \lesssim \| \nabla (A - B) \|_{L^2_x}. 
            \end{equation}
            Furthermore, fixing $\mathring A \in H^1_\mathrm{loc} (\mathbb R^2)$, perturbations by $a, b \in H^1 (\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:field-perturb-2}
                \bigl\| (F_{\mathring A + a})_{12} - (F_{\mathring A + b})_{12} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    \lesssim \| a - b \|_{H^1_x}. 
            \end{equation}

        \item Let $A - B, \Phi - \Psi \in H^1 (\mathbb R^2)$ 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:DA-perturb}
                \bigl\| {\bf D}_A \Phi - {\bf D}_B \Psi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    \lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \| \Phi \|_{L^4_x + L^\infty_x} + \| B \|_{L^4_x} \Bigr) \| (A, \Phi) - (B, \Psi) \|_{H^1_x}.
            \end{equation}
            Furthermore, fixing $(\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi}) \in H^1_\mathrm{loc} (\mathbb R^2)$, perturbations by $(a, u), (b, v) \in H^1 (\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:DA-perturb-2}
                \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\mathring A + a} (\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} + u) - {\bf D}_{\mathring A + b} (\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} + v) \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                    \lesssim \Bigl( \| \mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} \|_{L^4_x + L^\infty_x} + \| \mathring A \|_{L^4} + \| u \|_{L^4_x} + \| b \|_{L^4_x} \Bigr) \| (a, u) - (b, v) \|_{H^1_x}.
            \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-38 -->
<!-- proof-103: body_md -->
The magnetic field bounds (\ref{eq:field-perturb})-(\ref{eq:field-perturb-2}) are obvious by linearity, and the bounds (\ref{eq:charge-perturb-2}) and (\ref{eq:DA-perturb-2}) are immediate consequences of the previous (\ref{eq:charge-perturb}) and (\ref{eq:DA-perturb}) by the triangle inequality and Sobolev embedding. Writing 
        \[
            |\Phi|^2 - |\Psi|^2 = (|\Phi| + |\Psi|)(|\Phi| - |\Psi|),
        \] 
    and 
        \begin{align*}
            {\bf D}_A \Phi - {\bf D}_B \Psi 
                = \nabla(\Phi - \Psi) -i (A - B) \Phi - i B (\Phi - \Psi),
        \end{align*}
    the bounds (\ref{eq:charge-perturb}) and (\ref{eq:charge-perturb}) follow from H\"older's inequality, placing the coefficients in $L^4 + L^\infty$ and the differences in $L^4 \cap L^2$, and the Sobolev embedding.
<!-- end proof-103 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
Let $A = A_j \, dx^j$ and $B = B_j \, dx^j$ be connection $1$-forms, and let $\Phi$ be a complex scalar field. Then, for each non-negative integer $n \in \mathbb N_0$,  
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:schematic-D}
            {\bf D}_A^{(n + 1)} \Phi 
                = {\bf D}_B^{(n + 1)} \Phi + \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{a + b = k} \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi
        \end{equation}
    where $\nabla^{(\leq n)}$ denotes differentiation up to order $n$.
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-104: body_md -->
Clearly the expression holds for $n = 0$ by definition ${\bf D}_A = {\bf D}_B - i (A - B)$. Assume for induction then (\ref{eq:schematic-D}), then by the product rule, 
        \begin{align*}
            {\bf D}^{(n + 2)}_A \Phi 
                &= ({\bf D}_B - i (A - B)) \Bigl( {\bf D}_B^{(n + 1)} \Phi + \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{a + b = k} \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi \Bigr) \\
                &= {\bf D}_B^{(n + 2)} \Phi + \sum_{j + k = n + 1} \sum_{a + b = k} \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi.
        \end{align*}
    as desired.
<!-- end proof-104 -->
<!-- remark-26: body_md -->
In the schematic formula (\ref{eq:schematic-D}), one should think of the index $j$ as the number of factors of $A$, the index $k$ as the number of derivatives, and the indices $a$ and $b$ denoting the distribution of derivatives between the magnetic potentials and the scalar field respectively. Note the expression $(\nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B))^{j + 1}$ is rather inefficient with regards to the distribution of derivatives, but it will suffice for our purposes, as it succinctly captures the worst possible scenario where all the derivatives fall on one factor.
<!-- end remark-26 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer, $A = A_j \, dx^j$ and $B = B_j \, dx^j$ be connection $1$-forms, and $\Phi \in H^n_\mathrm{loc} (\mathbb R^2)$. 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item If $A - B \in H^{n} (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:equiv-HN}
                \Bigl( 1 + \| A - B \|_{H^{n - 1}}^{n} \Bigr)^{-1}  \| \Phi \|_{H^n_B} \lesssim \| \Phi \|_{H^n_A} \lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \| A - B \|_{H^n}^{n} \Bigr) \| \Phi \|_{H^n_B}.
            \end{equation}

        \item If $A \in L^4 (\mathbb R^2)$ and $\nabla A \in H^{n - 2} (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:equiv-HN-2}
                \Bigl( 1 + \| A \|_{L^4}^{n} + \| \nabla A \|_{H^{n - 2}}^n \Bigr)^{-1}  \| \Phi \|_{H^n} \lesssim \| \Phi \|_{H^n_A} \lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \| A \|_{L^4}^{n} + \| \nabla A \|_{H^{n - 2}}^n \Bigr) \| \Phi \|_{H^n}.
            \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-105: body_md -->
Appropriately applying H\"older and Sobolev embedding, e.g. (\ref{eq:GNinfty}) and (\ref{eq:GN-interpolation}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}_A \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| {\bf D}_B \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2} + \bigl\| A - B \bigr\|_{L^4} \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^4} \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \bigl\| A - B \bigr\|_{H^1} \Bigr) \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{H^1_B}, \\ 
            \bigl\| {\bf D}_A^{(2)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| {\bf D}_B^{(2)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2} + \bigl\| A - B \bigr\|_{L^4} \bigl\| {\bf D}_B \Phi \bigr\|_{L^4} + \bigl\| \nabla(A - B) \bigr\|_{L^2} \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty} + \bigl\| A - B \bigr\|_{L^4}^2 \|\Phi \|_{L^\infty} \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \bigl\| A - B \bigr\|_{H^1}^2 \Bigr) \bigl\| \Phi \bigr\|_{H^2_B}.
        \end{align*}
    The reverse inequality is a symmetric calculation. We can conclude (\ref{eq:equiv-HN}) for $n = 2$. 

    For higher-orders, assume for induction the result holds up to $n$. Again, by symmetry, it suffices to prove one direction of the inequality (\ref{eq:equiv-HN}). We estimate the schematic formula (\ref{eq:schematic-D}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 1)}_A \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| {\bf D}_B^{(n + 1)} \Phi  \bigr\|_{L^2} + \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{a + b = k} \Bigl\| \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi \Bigr\|_{L^2}.
        \end{align*}
    It remains to estimate the sum; we work case-by-case depending on how the derivatives are distributed. When all the derivatives fall on the magnetic potentials, i.e. $b = 0$, we may estimate using H\"older and Sobolev embedding (\ref{eq:GNinfty})
        \begin{align*}
            \sum_{j + k = n}\Bigl\| \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq k)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot \Phi \Bigr\|_{L^2}
                &\lesssim \| A - B \|_{H^n}^{n + 1} \|\Phi \|_{L^\infty} \\
                &\lesssim \| A - B \|_{H^n}^{n + 1} \| {\bf D}^{(2)}_B \Phi \|_{L^2}. 
        \end{align*}
    When the derivatives are distributed between the two, i.e. $b \neq 0$, then the number of derivatives hitting the difference of the magnetic potentials is at most $n - 1$. Thus, putting both factors in, say, $L^4$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{\substack{a + b = k \\ b \neq 0}} \Bigl\| \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi \Bigr\|_{L^2}.
                &\lesssim \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{\substack{a + b = k \\ b \neq 0}}  \bigl\| (\nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B))^{j + 1} \bigr\|_{L^4} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(b)}_B \Phi \bigr\|_{L^4} \\
                &\lesssim \| A - B \|_{H^n}^{n} \| \Phi \|_{H^{n + 1}_B},  
        \end{align*}
    using Sobolev embedding wherever appropriate.
<!-- end proof-105 -->
<!-- proof-106: body_md -->
Following the proof of (\ref{eq:equiv-HN}) and taking $B \equiv 0$, it is not difficult to see the result holds for $n = 2$. For higher-orders, assume for induction the result holds up to $n$. By symmetry, it suffices to prove one direction of the inequality (\ref{eq:equiv-HN-2}). We estimate the schematic formula (\ref{eq:schematic-D}), 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n + 1)}_A \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \nabla^{(n + 1)} \Phi  \bigr\|_{L^2} + \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{a + b = k} \Bigl\| \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} A \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot \nabla^{(b)} \Phi \Bigr\|_{L^2}.
        \end{align*}
    When all the derivatives fall on the scalar field, i.e. $a = 0$, using H\"older and Sobolev embedding yields
        \begin{align*}
            \sum_{j + k = n} \Bigl\| A^{j + 1} \cdot \nabla^{(k)} \Phi \Bigr\|_{L^2}
                &\lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \| A \|_{L^4}^{n + 1} \Bigr) \| \Phi\|_{H^{n + 1}}.
        \end{align*}
    When the derivatives are distributed between the two, i.e. $a \neq 0$, we can put both factors in, say, $L^4$ and estimate using Sobolev embedding
        \begin{align*}
            \sum_{j + k = n}\sum_{\substack{a + b = k \\ a \neq 0}} \Bigl\| \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} A \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot \nabla^{(b)} \Phi \Bigr\|_{L^2}
                &\lesssim  \sum_{j + k = n}\sum_{\substack{a + b = k \\ a \neq 0}} \bigl\| \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} A \bigr)^{j + 1} \bigr\|_{L^4} \bigl\| \nabla^{(b)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^4} \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \| \nabla A \|_{H^n}^{n + 1} \Bigr) \| \Phi \|_{H^{n + 1}}.
        \end{align*}
    This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-106 -->
<!-- proposition-39: body_md -->
\label{prop:magnetic-lip-2}
    Let $n \in \mathbb N_0$ be a non-negative integer, $A \equiv A_j \, dx^j$ and $B \equiv B_j \, dx^j$ be connection $1$-forms such that $A, B \in L^4 (\mathbb R^2)$ and $\nabla A, \nabla B \in H^{n - 1} (\mathbb R^2)$, and let $\Phi \in X^{n + 1}_A (\mathbb R^2)$ and $\Psi \in X^{n + 1}_B (\mathbb R^2)$. Suppose also that $A - B \in H^n (\mathbb R^2)$ and $\Phi - \Psi \in H^{n + 1} (\mathbb R^2)$, then  
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:magn-perturb}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}_A^{(n + 1)} \Phi - {\bf D}_B^{(n + 1)}\Psi \bigr\|_{L^2}
                \leq C_n \cdot \Bigl( \|A - B \|_{H^n} + \| \Phi - \Psi \|_{H^{n + 1}} \Bigr),
        \end{equation}
    where the constant depends on 
        \[
            C_n 
                \equiv C_n \bigl( \| A \|_{L^4}, \| \nabla A \|_{H^{n - 1}}, \| A - B \|_{H^{n}}, \| \Phi \|_{X^n_A}\bigr).
        \]
    Furthermore, fixing $(\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi})$ satisfying $\mathring A \in L^4 (\mathbb R^2)$ and $\nabla \mathring A \in H^{n - 1} (\mathbb R^2)$ and $\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} \in H^n_{\mathring A} (\mathbb R^2)$, perturbations by perturbations by $(a, u), (b, v) \in (H^n \times H^{n + 1}) (\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:magn-perturb-2}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\mathring A + a}^{(n + 1)} (\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} + u) - {\bf D}_{\mathring A + b}^{(n + 1)} (\mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} + v) \bigr\|_{L^2} 
                \lesssim C_n\cdot \|(a, u) - (b, v) \|_{H^n \times H^{n + 1}},
        \end{equation}
    where the constant depends on 
        \[
            C_n \equiv C_n \bigl( \| \mathring A \|_{L^4}, \| \nabla \mathring A \|_{H^{n - 1}}, \| \mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi} \|_{X^{n}_{\mathring A}}, \| (a, u) \|_{H^n \times X^{n}}, \| (b, v) \|_{H^n \times X^{n}}  \bigr).
        \]
<!-- end proposition-39 -->
<!-- proof-107: body_md -->
The bound (\ref{eq:magn-perturb-2}) is an consequence of (\ref{eq:magn-perturb}), taking 
        \[
            (A, \Phi) = (\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi}) + (a, u), \qquad (B, \Psi) = (\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A} \Phi}) + (b, v),
        \]
    and then carefully estimating the constants appropriately. We leave this easy verification to the reader. 

    By slightly modifying the proof of (\ref{eq:DA-perturb}), placing the scalar field in $L^\infty$ rather than $L^4 + L^\infty$, we may obtain the $n = 0$ case. From here, we proceed by induction, assuming the result up to $n - 1$. Using the schematic identity (\ref{eq:schematic-D}), we may rewrite everything in terms of magnetic derivatives with respect to $B$, which yields 
        \begin{align*}
            {\bf D}_A^{(n + 1)} \Phi - {\bf D}_B^{{(n + 1)}} \Psi 
                &= {\bf D}_B^{(n + 1)} (\Phi - \Psi) + \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{a + b = k} \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi.
        \end{align*}
    Putting the above in $L^2$, the first term on the right is acceptable in view of (\ref{eq:equiv-HN}). For the second term on the right, when all the derivatives fall on the magnetic potentials, i.e. $b = 0$, we may estimate using H\"older and Sobolev embedding
        \begin{align*}
            \sum_{j + k = n} \bigl\| \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq k)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| A - B \bigr\|_{H^{n}}^{n + 1} \| \Phi \|_{L^\infty}.
        \end{align*}
    When all the derivatives fall on the scalar field, i.e. $a = 0$, we similarly have
        \begin{align*}
            \sum_{j +k = n} \bigl\| (A - B)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}^{(k)}_B\Phi\bigr\|_{L^2}
                &\lesssim \sum_{j + k = n}\| A - B \|_{L^\infty_x}^{j + 1} \| {\bf D}^{(k)}_B \Phi \|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( 1 + \| A - B \|_{H^n_x}^{n + 1} \Bigr) \Bigl( \sum_{k = 1}^n  \| {\bf D}^{(k)}_B \Phi \|_{L^2_x}\Bigr) \\
                &\lesssim C_n \Bigl( 1 + \| A - B \|_{H^n_x}^{n + 1} \Bigr) \Bigl( \sum_{k = 1}^n  \| {\bf D}^{(k)}_A \Phi \|_{L^2_x}\Bigr),
        \end{align*}
    using the induction hypothesis in the last line. When at least one derivative falls on both the magnetic potentials and the scalar fields, i.e. $a, b \neq 0$, then at most $n - 1$ derivatives falls on any given factor. Placing both in $L^4$ and using Sobolev embedding, 
        \begin{align*}
            \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{\substack{a + b = k \\ a, b \neq 0}} \Bigl\|  \bigl( \nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B) \bigr)^{j + 1} \cdot {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi \Bigr\|_{L^2} 
                &\lesssim \sum_{j + k = n} \sum_{\substack{a + b = k \\ b \neq 0}}  \bigl\| (\nabla^{(\leq a)} (A - B))^{j + 1}\bigr\|_{L^4}\bigl\| {\bf D}_B^{(b)} \Phi \bigr\|_{L^{4}} \\
                &\lesssim \Bigl( 1 +  \| A - B \|_{H^{n}}^{n + 1} \Bigr) \sum_{k = 1}^n \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(k)}_B \Phi \bigr\|_{L^2}\\
                &\lesssim C_n \Bigl( 1 + \| A - B \|_{H^n_x}^{n + 1} \Bigr) \Bigl( \sum_{k = 1}^n  \| {\bf D}^{(k)}_A \Phi \|_{L^2_x}\Bigr),
        \end{align*}
    again using the induction hypothesis in the last line. Collecting the previous inequalities, we conclude the result.
<!-- end proof-107 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:picard}
    Let $(\mathring A, \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}) \in \mathfrak E^\infty$ be a smooth configuration in Coulomb gauge (\ref{eq:coulomb-data}), and suppose that $(A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}) \in \mathfrak I^{9000}$. Set
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:high-data}
            \mathsf E 
                := \mathcal E^{9000} [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^\mathrm{in}].
        \end{equation}
    Then there exists a positive time $T \equiv T(\mathsf E)$ and a solution $(A, \phi) \in \mathfrak S^{9000}([0, T])$ to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation in DeTurck gauge (\ref{eq:CSS-DT-intro}) with initial data $(A, \phi)_{|t = 0} = (A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}})$. 

    Furthermore, if $(A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}) \in \mathfrak I^\infty$, then $(A, \phi)$ is a smooth solution to the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:CSS-DT}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ solving the Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:CSS-amp-schro}) in DeTurck gauge (\ref{eq:DeTurck}). Then the magnetic potential satisfies the heat equation
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:A-DT}
            (\partial_t - \Delta) A_j 
                = - \varepsilon_{jk} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi) + \Bigl( \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) + \partial_j \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \Bigr) + \varepsilon_{\ell j} \Bigl( \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^\ell \phi) + \partial^\ell \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \Bigr).
        \end{equation}
    Furthermore, the curl-free and divergence-free parts satisfy the schematic equations 
        \begin{align}
            (\partial_t - \Delta) \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A 
                &= \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} (\phi \cdot {\bf D} \phi) + \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,,\label{eq:A-DT-cf}\\ 
            \Delta \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} A 
                &= \nabla^\perp \bigl( \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) + \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr). \label{eq:A-DT-df}
        \end{align}
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-108: body_md -->
Using the DeTurck gauge, we can write $\partial^\ell F_{\ell j} = \Delta A_j - \partial_j A_t$. Inserting this into Amp\'ere's law, 
        \begin{align*}
            (\partial_t - \Delta) A_j 
                &= F_{tj} - \partial^\ell F_{\ell j} \\
                &= - \varepsilon_{jk} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi) - \partial_j F_{12} - \partial^\ell F_{\ell j} \\
                &= - \varepsilon_{jk} \operatorname{Im}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^k \phi) + \Bigl( \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}_j \phi) + \partial_j \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \Bigr) + \varepsilon_{\ell j} \Bigl( \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi {\bf D}^\ell \phi) + \partial^\ell \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \Bigr),
        \end{align*}
    rewriting instances of the magnetic field in terms of the scalar field and the Gauss tension field. Projecting onto curl-free vector fields, we obtain the desired parabolic equation (\ref{eq:A-DT-cf}) for the curl-free part. The elliptic equation (\ref{eq:A-DT-df}) for the divergence-free part is precisely the Biot-Savart law.
<!-- end proof-108 -->
<!-- proposition-40: body_md -->
\label{prop:iterate-energy}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ satisfying
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:prev-iterate}
            \Bigl( i \partial_t + \bigl( {\bf D}_A\bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_A \bigr)_j + \mathsf V \Bigr) \phi 
                = 0,
        \end{equation}
    for some real-valued potential $\mathsf V :[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R$, and the energy bound 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:prev-iterate-energy}
            \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \slashed\mathcal E^{9000} [A(t), \phi(t)] 
                \leq 2 \mathsf E. 
        \end{equation}
    Then there exists a sufficiently small time $T \ll_\mathsf E 1$ such that the solution $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi)$ on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ to the system (\ref{eq:iterationeq}) satisfies 
        \begin{itemize}
            \item the magnetic energy bound 
                \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-energy}
                      \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \slashed\mathcal E^{9000} [\widehat A(t), \widehat \phi(t)] 
                \leq 2 \mathsf E. 
                \end{equation}

            \item the top-order Sobolev bound for the magnetic potential, 
                \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-A-HN-top}
                    \bigl\| \nabla  \widehat A \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t H^{8999}_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(2)} \widehat A \bigr\|_{L^2_t H^{8999}_x}
                \lesssim 1 + \bigl\| \nabla A^{\mathrm{in}} \bigr\|_{H^{8999}_x},
                \end{equation}

            \item the bottom-order affine Sobolev estimate for the magnetic potential, 
                \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-A-HN-bot}
                    \bigl\| \widehat A - \mathring A\bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} 
                        \lesssim 1 + \bigl\| A^{\mathrm{in}} - \mathring A \bigr\|_{L^2_x}.
                \end{equation}
                \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-40 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ and let $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi)$ be a solution to the system (\ref{eq:iterationeq}). Then the charge density of $\widehat \phi$ satisfies the density-flux relation
        \begin{align}\label{eq:iterate-charge-transport}
            \partial_t \tfrac12 (1 - |\widehat \phi|^2) 
                = \nabla ( \widehat \phi \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi).
        \end{align}
    Furthermore, if $(A, \phi)$ satisfies (\ref{eq:prev-iterate}), then the divergence-free part of $\widehat A$ obeys the transport equation,
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-transport}
            \partial_t \widehat{A^\mathrm{df}}
                = \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} (\phi \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi).
        \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-109: body_md -->
Differentiating the charge density and using the Schr\"odinger equation for $\widehat \phi$ and the product rule, 
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_t \tfrac12(1 - |\widehat \phi|^2) 
                &= - \operatorname{Re}\bigl( \overline{\widehat \phi} \partial_t \widehat \phi \bigr) \\
                &= \operatorname{Im}\Bigl(\overline{\widehat \phi} \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)_j \widehat \phi \Bigr) \\
                &= \partial^j \operatorname{Im}\Bigl(\overline{\widehat \phi}  \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)_j \widehat \phi \Bigr) = \nabla \bigl( \widehat \phi \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi \bigr),
        \end{align*}
    yielding (\ref{eq:iterate-charge-transport}). 
    
    Differentiating the elliptic equation for the divergence-free part in (\ref{eq:iterationeq}), using the Schr\"odinger equation for $\phi$ and the product rule, 
        \begin{align*}
            \partial_t  \widehat{A^\mathrm{df}} 
                &= \nabla^{-1} \operatorname{Re}(\overline \phi \partial_t \phi) \\
                &=\nabla^{-1} \operatorname{Im}\Bigl( \overline \phi \bigl( {\bf D}_{A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{A}\bigr)_j \phi \Bigr) \\
                &= \nabla^{-1} \partial^j \operatorname{Im}\Bigl( \overline \phi ({\bf D}_A)_j \phi \Bigr) = \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} (\overline \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi), 
        \end{align*}
    yielding (\ref{eq:iterate-transport})
<!-- end proof-109 -->
<!-- remark-27: body_md -->
For the first Picard iterate $(\widehat A^{[1]}, \widehat \phi^{[1]})$, instead of (\ref{eq:iterate-transport}) we can use the simpler transport equation 
        \[
            \partial_t \widehat A^{[1]} = 0. 
        \]
<!-- end remark-27 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ satisfying (\ref{eq:prev-iterate}), and suppose $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi)$ is a solution to the system (\ref{eq:iterationeq}). Then, for each positive integer $n \in \mathbb N$, 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item the scalar field obeys the Schr\"odinger equation,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-schro}
            \begin{split}
                \Bigl( i \partial_t + \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell + \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A}\bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(n)} \widehat\phi
                    &= {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(n)} \widehat \phi + \sum_{a + b + c = n} \mathbb P \bigl({\bf D}_A^{(a)} \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A^{(b)} \phi\bigr) \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(c)} \widehat \phi \\
                        &\qquad + \sum_{a + b = n} \mathbb P \bigl(\nabla^{(a)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,\bigr) \cdot {\bf D}_A^{(b)} \widehat \phi,
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}
        where $\mathbb P$ is a Fourier multiplier of order zero,
        
        \item the curl-free part of the magnetic potential obeys the heat equation,
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-heat}
                (\partial_t - \Delta) \nabla^{(n)}  \widehat{A^\mathrm{cf}} 
                    = \nabla \Bigl( \sum_{a + b = n} {\bf D}_A^{(a)} \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A^{(b)} \phi + \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \Bigr),
            \end{equation}
        
        \item the divergence-free part of the magnetic potential obeys
            \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-elliptic}
            \begin{split}
                \nabla  \widehat{A^\mathrm{df}} 
                    &= \tfrac12(1 - |\phi|^2) + \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,, \\ 
                \nabla^{(n)}  \widehat{A^\mathrm{df}} 
                    &= 
                        \sum_{a + b = n - 1} {\bf D}^{(a)}_A \cdot {\bf D}^{(b)}_A \phi + \nabla^{(n - 1)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,, \qquad \text{for $n \geq 2$.}
            \end{split}
            \end{equation}

    \end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-110: body_md -->
Commuting,  
        \begin{align*}
            \Bigl[ {\bf D}_{\widehat A} , \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr) ({\bf D}_{\widehat A}) + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr]
                &= \widehat F_{12} \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A} + \nabla \widehat F_{12} + \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi \\
                &= {\bf D}_{\widehat A} + \phi \cdot \phi \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A} + \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A} + \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, + \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi,
            \end{align*}
    using the elliptic equation for the divergence-free part to rewrite the magnetic field. The commutator with the magnetic time derivative is given by  
        \begin{align*}
            \Bigl[ ({\bf D}_{\widehat A})_k, i \partial_t + \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell \Bigr]
                &= \partial_t \widehat A_k -  \partial_k \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell  \\
                &= (\partial_t - \Delta) (\mathbb P^\mathrm{cf}_k \widehat A + \mathbb P^\mathrm{df}_k \widehat A) + \varepsilon_{jk} \partial^j \widehat F_{12} \\
                &= \mathbb P (\phi \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi) + \mathbb P \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,,
            \end{align*}
    using the heat equation for the curl-free part, the elliptic equation for the divergence-free part from (\ref{eq:iterationeq}), and the transport equation (\ref{eq:iterate-transport}) for the divergence-free part to re-express its time-derivative.

    With these two commutator identities at hand, we can easily show (\ref{eq:iterate-schro}) by induction. Indeed, the case $n = 1$ is immediate from commuting ${\bf D}_{\widehat A}$ into (\ref{eq:iterationeq}); proceeding inductively, we apply ${\bf D}_{\widehat A}$ to the equation for $n$. The right-hand side is acceptable due to the product rule, while the commutators from the left are also easily seen to be of the desired form by the calculations above.
<!-- end proof-110 -->
<!-- proof-111: body_md -->
The proof will follow a similar argument to that of the covariant energy estimate (\ref{eq:EN-bound-1}), plus estimating the $L^\infty$-norms of the scalar fields by the Sobolev-type inequality (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}). For these reason, we will be brief with writing out all the details. Making the bootstrap assumption
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:BS-iterate}
            \sup_{t \in [0, T]}\slashed\mathcal E^N [\widehat A(t), \widehat \phi(t)] 
                \leq 10\mathsf E,
        \end{equation}
    our goal is to improve the bound to $2\mathsf E$. Throughout, we denote $C(\mathsf E)$ for some polynomial expression in $\mathsf E$, the definition of which may change line-by-line.
    
    Multiplying the transport equation (\ref{eq:iterate-charge-transport}) by the charge density, and integrating-by-parts, we obtain
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-charge-est}
        \begin{split}
            \bigl\| \tfrac12 (1 - |\widehat \phi|^2) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}^2
                &\leq \bigl\| \tfrac12(1 - |\phi^{\mathrm{in}}|^2) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 + T \cdot \bigl\| \widehat \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, x}}^2 \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}^2 \\
                &\leq \bigl\| \tfrac12(1 - |\phi^{\mathrm{in}}|^2) \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2 + T \cdot C(\mathsf E) ,
        \end{split}
        \end{equation}
    using the bootstrap assumption (\ref{eq:BS-iterate}) and the Sobolev-type inequality (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}) in the second line. 

    To control magnetic energy, we apply the abstract energy estimate (\ref{eq:abstract-energy}) to the Schr\"odinger equation (\ref{eq:iterate-schro}), and estimate the right-hand side. The linear term is easily treated, while for the non-linear terms, we can use H\"older's inequality, the magnetic interpolation inequalities (\ref{eq:GN-interpolation}), and the Sobolev-type inequality (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}), and the bootstrap assumption (\ref{eq:BS-iterate}),
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \text{R.H.S. (\ref{eq:iterate-schro})} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + \sum_{a + b + c = n}\bigl\| {\bf D}^{(a)}_A \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/a}_x} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(b)}_A \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/b}_x} \, \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(c)}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/c}_x}\\
                &\qquad +  \sum_{a + b = n} \bigl\| \nabla^{(a)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\,  \bigr\|_{L^{2n/a}_x} \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} ^{(b)} \widehat \phi  \bigr\|_{L^{2n/b}_x} \\
                &\lesssim C(\mathsf E).
        \end{align*}
    Inserting this into the energy estimate (\ref{eq:abstract-energy}) for (\ref{eq:iterate-schro}),
        \begin{equation} \label{eq:iterate-Dphi-est}
        \begin{split}
            \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(n)} \widehat \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2}^2 
                &\leq \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)}_{A^{\mathrm{in}}} \phi^{\mathrm{in}} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2  + T \cdot  \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(n)} \widehat \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \bigl\| \text{R.H.S. (\ref{eq:iterate-schro})} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \\ 
                &\leq \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(n)}_{A^{\mathrm{in}}} \phi^{\mathrm{in}} \bigr\|_{L^2_x}^2  + T \cdot C(\mathsf E). 
        \end{split}
        \end{equation}

    Putting together the estimates (\ref{eq:iterate-charge-est}) and (\ref{eq:iterate-Dphi-est}) for $n = 1, \dots, 9000$, we obtain 
        \begin{align*}
            \sup_{t \in [0, T]}\slashed\mathcal E^{9000} [\widehat A(t), \widehat \phi(t)]
                &\leq \slashed\mathcal E^{9000}  [A^{\mathrm{in}}, \phi^{\mathrm{in}}] + T \cdot C(\mathsf E) \leq 2 \mathsf E,
        \end{align*}
    taking $T \ll_\mathsf E 1$. This closes the bootstrap (\ref{eq:BS-iterate}).
<!-- end proof-111 -->
<!-- proof-112: body_md -->
Applying the energy estimate (\ref{eq:heat-energy-estimate}) to the heat equation for the curl-free part (\ref{eq:iterate-heat}), using interpolation (\ref{eq:GN-interpolation}) and the Sobolev-type estimate (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}) wherever appropriate, 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)}  \widehat{A^\mathrm{cf}} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(n + 1)}  \widehat{A^\mathrm{cf}} \bigr\|_{L^2_{t, x}}
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A^{\mathrm{in}} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                    &\qquad + \Bigl\| \sum_{a + b = n} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(a)}_A \phi  \bigr\|_{L^{2n/a}_x} \bigl\| {\bf D}_A^{(b)} \phi \bigr\|_{L^{2n/b}_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x}\Bigr\|_{L^2_t} \\
                    &\lesssim \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A^{\mathrm{in}} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                        &\qquad+ T^\frac12 \Bigl( \bigl( \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} + \| {\bf D}_A \phi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \bigr) \| {\bf D}^{(n)}_A \phi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x}\Bigr) \\
                    &\lesssim \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} A^{\mathrm{in}} \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + T^\frac12 \cdot C(\mathsf E)
        \end{align*}
    for each $n = 1, \dots, N$. Similarly estimating the expressions (\ref{eq:iterate-elliptic}) for the divergence-free part gives 
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \nabla \widehat{A^\mathrm{df}} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}
                &\lesssim\bigl\| \tfrac12 (1 - |\phi|^2) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim C(\mathsf E), \\
            \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \nabla  \widehat{A^\mathrm{df}} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \sum_{a + b = n} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(a)}_A \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^{2n/a}_x} \bigl\| {\bf D}^{(b)}_A \phi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^{2n/b}_x} + \bigl\| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \bigr\|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim \bigl( \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \| {\bf D}_A \phi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \bigr) \| {\bf D}^{(n)}_A \phi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \| \nabla^{(n)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim C(\mathsf E),
        \end{align*}
    for each $n = 1, \dots, 9000$. Collecting these inequalities and taking $T \ll_\mathsf E 1$ gives the top-order estimate (\ref{eq:iterate-A-HN-top}). 

    Integrating the transport equation (\ref{eq:iterate-transport}) and the heat equation (\ref{eq:iterate-heat}) in time and estimating the right-hand side using the magnetic energy estimates (\ref{eq:iterate-energy}) and Sobolev embedding,
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \widehat A - \mathring A \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| A^{\mathrm{in}} - \mathring A \bigr\|_{L^2_x} +\bigl\| \Delta \mathbb P^{\mathrm{cf}} \widehat A \bigr\|_{L^1_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi \bigr\|_{L^1_t L^2_x} \\
                &\lesssim  \bigl\| A^{\mathrm{in}} - \mathring A \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + T \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\| \nabla^{(2)} \mathbb P^{\mathrm{cf}} \widehat A \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} +  \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \| {\bf D}_A \phi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr) \\
                &\lesssim  \bigl\| A^{\mathrm{in}} - \mathring A \bigr\|_{L^2_x} + T \cdot C(\mathsf E).
        \end{align*}
    using the top-order bound (\ref{eq:iterate-A-HN-top}) to control the derivatives of the curl-free part of the magnetic potential. Taking $T \ll_\mathsf E 1$, we conclude the bottom-order affine Sobolev estimate (\ref{eq:iterate-A-HN-bot}).
<!-- end proof-112 -->
<!-- proposition-41: body_md -->
\label{prop:linear-LWP}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ be a configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ satisfying the energy bound (\ref{eq:prev-iterate-energy}). Then there exists $T \ll_\mathsf E 1$ and a solution $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi) \in \mathfrak S^{9000} ([0, T])$ to the system (\ref{eq:iterationeq}) satisfying 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-phi-affine}
            \bigl\| \widehat \phi- \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi} \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t H^{9000}_x}
                \lesssim_{\mathsf E, \mathsf A} \bigl\| \phi^{\mathrm{in}} - \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi} \bigr\|_{H^{9000}_x}.
        \end{equation}
    and 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:iterate-A-affine}
            \bigl\| \widehat A - \mathring A\bigr\|_{L^\infty_t H^{9000}_x} + \bigl\| \nabla(\widehat A - \mathring A)\bigr\|_{L^2_t H^{9000}_x}
                \lesssim_{\mathsf E, \mathsf A} 1.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-41 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
Let $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi)$ be the configuration on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ solving the system (\ref{eq:iterationeq}), and set $u := \widehat \phi - \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}$. Then the perturbation $u : [0, T] \times \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb C$ satisfies the linear inhomogeneous Schr\"odinger equation 
        \begin{equation}\label{eq:perturb-base}
            \Bigl( i \partial_t + \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell + \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A}\bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) u 
                = \Bigl( \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell + \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A}\bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi}, 
        \end{equation}
    Furthermore, for each positive integer $n \in \mathbb N$, we have the higher-order equation 
        \begin{align}
            \Bigl( i \partial_t + \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell + \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A}\bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(n)} u
                &= {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(n)} u + \sum_{a + b + c = n} \mathbb P \bigl({\bf D}_A^{(a)} \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A^{(b)} \phi\bigr) \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(c)} u \notag\\
                    &\qquad + \sum_{a + b = n} \mathbb P \nabla^{(a)} \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat A}^{(b)} u \label{eq:perturb-high} \\
                    &\qquad + {\bf D}^{(n)}_{\widehat A} \Bigl( \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell + \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A}\bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) \mathring{\vphantom{A}\phi} ,\notag
        \end{align}
    where $\mathbb P$ is a Fourier multiplier of order zero.
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
Suppose $\widehat A \in \mathring A + L^\infty_t H^N_x (\mathbb R^2)$, then 
        \begin{align}\label{eq:iterate-equiv}
            \| u \|_{L^\infty_t H^N_{\widehat A}} 
                \sim_{\mathsf E, \mathsf A} \|u \|_{L^\infty_t H^N_x} \sim_\mathsf A \| u \|_{L^\infty_t H^N_{\mathring A}}.
        \end{align}
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-113: body_md -->
This follows from (\ref{eq:equiv-HN})-(\ref{eq:equiv-HN-2}), using (\ref{eq:iterate-A-affine}) and (\ref{eq:background-bound}) to control the implicit constant.
<!-- end proof-113 -->
<!-- proposition-42: body_md -->
\label{prop:high-contract}
    Let $(A, \phi)$ and $(B, \psi)$ be configurations on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ satisfying the equation (\ref{eq:prev-iterate}) and the bounds (\ref{eq:prev-iterate-energy}), and suppose $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi)$ and $(\widehat B, \widehat \psi)$ are the corresponding solutions to the system (\ref{eq:iterationeq}). Then there exists a sufficiently small $T \ll_\mathsf E 1$ such that 
        \begin{equation}
            \bigl\| (\widehat A ,\widehat \phi) - (\widehat B, \widehat \psi) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t (L^2 \times H^1)_x}
                \leq \tfrac12 \bigl\| (A, \phi) - (B, \psi) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t (L^2 \times H^1)_x}.
        \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-42 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
Let $(A, \phi)$ and $(B, \psi)$ be configurations on $[0, T] \times \mathbb R^2$ satisfying (\ref{eq:prev-iterate}), and suppose $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi)$ and $(\widehat B, \widehat \psi)$ are solutions to the system (\ref{eq:iterationeq}). Then 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item the scalar field differences obey the Schr\"odinger equations
            \begin{align}
            \begin{split}
                \Bigl( i \partial_t + \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell &+ \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) \bigl(\widehat\phi - \widehat\psi\bigr) \\
                    &= \Bigl( \nabla \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} \bigl(\widehat A - \widehat B\bigr) + \bigl( \widehat A \cdot \widehat A - \widehat B \cdot \widehat B \bigr)+ \bigl( \phi \cdot \phi - \psi \cdot \psi \bigr)\Bigr) \cdot \widehat \psi \\
                    &\qquad + \bigl( \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr) \cdot \nabla \widehat \psi,
            \end{split}\label{eq:iterate-schro-diff}
            \end{align}
            and 
            \begin{equation}
                \begin{split}
                \Bigl( i \partial_t + \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell &+ \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) \bigl({\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat\psi\bigr)\\
                    &= \Bigl( \nabla \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} \bigl(\widehat A - \widehat B\bigr) + \bigl( \widehat A \cdot \widehat A - \widehat B \cdot \widehat B \bigr)+ \bigl( \phi \cdot \phi - \psi \cdot \psi \bigr)\Bigr) \cdot {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \\
                    &\qquad + \bigl( \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr) \cdot \nabla {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat\psi + \Bigl( 1 + \phi \cdot \phi + \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A}  \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \Bigr) \\
                    &\qquad + \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \cdot \bigl( \widehat \phi - \widehat \psi \bigr) + \Bigl( \phi \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi \cdot \widehat \phi - \psi \cdot {\bf D}_B \psi \cdot \widehat \psi \Bigr),
            \end{split}\label{eq:iterate-schro-diff-2}
            \end{equation} 

        \item the curl-free differences of the magnetic potentials obey the heat equations
            \begin{align}
                 (\partial_t - \Delta) \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} \bigl(\widehat A - \widehat B\bigr)
                    &= \mathbb P \Bigl( (\phi - \psi) \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi + \psi \cdot ({\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi) \Bigr),\label{eq:iterate-heat-diff}
            \end{align}


        \item the divergence-free differences of the magnetic potentials obey
            \begin{align}
            \partial_t \mathbb P^\mathrm{df} \bigl(\widehat A - \widehat B\bigr) 
                &= \mathbb P \Bigl( (\phi - \psi) \cdot {\bf D}_A \phi + \psi \cdot({\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi) \Bigr).\label{eq:iterate-transport-diff}
            \end{align}

    \end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- proof-114: body_md -->
Taking the differences of the operators on the left-hand sides, 
        \begin{align*}
            \Bigl( \partial^\ell \widehat A_\ell &+ \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\phi|^2) \Bigr) - \Bigl( \partial^\ell \widehat B_\ell + \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \bigr)^j \bigl( {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \bigr)_j + \tfrac\lambda2 (1 - |\psi|^2) \Bigr) \\
                &= \Bigl( \partial^\ell (\widehat A_\ell - \widehat B_\ell) + i \partial^j (\widehat B_j - \widehat A_j) + (\widehat B^j \widehat B_j - \widehat A^j \widehat A_j) \Bigr)  + 2i \bigl(\widehat B^j - \widehat A^j\bigr) \partial_j + \tfrac\lambda2(|\psi|^2 - |\phi|^2) .
        \end{align*}
    Subtracting the equations (\ref{eq:iterate-schro}) for $(\widehat A, \widehat \phi)$ and $(\widehat B, \widehat \psi)$ for $n = 0, 1$ respectively and using the identity above gives the desired equations.
<!-- end proof-114 -->
<!-- proof-115: body_md -->
These follow from subtracting the respective heat equations (\ref{eq:iterate-heat}) and transport equations (\ref{eq:iterate-transport}).
<!-- end proof-115 -->
<!-- proof-116: body_md -->
It will suffice to show a bound of the form
        \begin{align}\label{eq:iterate-magn-diff}
            \bigl\| (\widehat A, \widehat \phi) - (\widehat B, \widehat \psi) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} 
                \lesssim_\mathcal E T \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\|  \phi - \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| {\bf D}_A  \phi - {\bf D}_{B} \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr).
        \end{align}
    Indeed, the left-hand side controls the $(L^2 \times H^1)$-difference, writing
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \nabla(\widehat \phi - \widehat \psi) \bigr\|_{L^2}
                &\leq \bigl\| \widehat A \cdot \widehat \phi - \widehat B \cdot \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^2} +  \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^2} \\
                &\leq \bigl\| \widehat A \bigr\|_{L^\infty} \bigl\| \widehat \phi - \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^2} + \bigl\| \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr\|_{L^2}\bigl\| \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_x} +  \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^2}\\
                &\lesssim_\mathsf E \bigl\| \widehat \phi - \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^2}  + \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^2} + \bigl\| \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr\|_{L^2_x},
        \end{align*}
    and on the right-hand side, we may bound the difference of the magnetic derivatives by
        \begin{align*}
            \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^2} + \bigl\| {\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi \bigr\|_{L^2}
                &\leq \| \phi - \psi\|_{H^1} + \| A \cdot \phi - B \cdot \psi \|_{L^2} \\
                &\leq \| \phi - \psi \|_{H^1} + \| A \|_{L^\infty} \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^2} + \| A - B \|_{L^2} \| \psi \|_{L^\infty} \\ 
                &\lesssim_\mathsf E \| \phi - \psi \|_{H^1} + \| A - B \|_{L^2},
        \end{align*}
    using energy estimates to bound the coefficients. Collecting these three inequalities, we conclude
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| (\widehat A, \widehat \phi) - (\widehat B, \widehat \psi) \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t (L^2 \times H^1)_x}
                \lesssim_\mathsf E T \cdot \| (A, \phi) - (B, \psi) \|_{L^\infty_t (L^2 \times H^1)_x}.
        \end{align*}
    Taking $T \ll_\mathsf E 1$ gives the result.             

    To estimate the $L^2$-difference of the magnetic potentials, integrate the transport equation for the difference of the divergence-free parts (\ref{eq:iterate-transport-diff}), and apply the energy estimate (\ref{eq:heat-energy-estimate}) to the heat equation for the difference of the curl-free parts (\ref{eq:iterate-heat-diff}). All together, these yield
        \begin{align}
            \bigl\| \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} +  \bigl\| \nabla \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} \bigl( \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr) \bigr\|_{L^2_{t, x}} 
                &\lesssim \bigl\| \text{R.H.S. (\ref{eq:iterate-heat-diff})} \bigr\|_{L^1_t L^2_x} \notag\\
                &\lesssim T \cdot \Bigl( \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \| {\bf D}_A \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} + \| \psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \| {\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr) \label{eq:iterate-diff-A}\\
                &\lesssim_\mathsf E T \cdot\Bigl( \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \| {\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr) . \notag
        \end{align}
    
    To control the differences of the scalar fields, we apply the energy estimate (\ref{eq:abstract-energy}) to the Schr\"odinger equations for the differences of the scalar fields (\ref{eq:iterate-schro-diff}) and their magnetic derivatives (\ref{eq:iterate-schro-diff-2}),
        \begin{align*}
            \bigl\| \widehat \phi - \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}
                &\lesssim \| \text{R.H.S. (\ref{eq:iterate-schro-diff})} \|_{L^1_t L^2_x} + \| \text{R.H.S. (\ref{eq:iterate-schro-diff-2})} \|_{L^1_t L^2_x}.
        \end{align*}
    We estimate the right-hand side by 
        \begin{align*}
             \| \text{R.H.S. (\ref{eq:iterate-schro-diff})} \|_{L^1_t L^2_x} 
                &\lesssim T\cdot \Bigl( \bigl( \| \widehat A \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} + \| \widehat B \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \bigr) \bigl\| \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl( \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} + \|\psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \bigr) \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr) \bigl\| \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \\
                    &\qquad + T^\frac12 \bigl\| \nabla \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} ( \widehat A - \widehat B) \bigr\|_{L^2_{t, x}} \bigl\| \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \\
                    &\qquad + T \bigl\| \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \bigl\| \nabla \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \\
                &\lesssim_\mathsf E T \cdot \Bigl(  \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \| {\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr),
        \end{align*}
    and similarly,
        \begin{align*}
             \| \text{R.H.S. (\ref{eq:iterate-schro-diff-2})} \|_{L^1_t L^2_x}
                &\lesssim T\cdot \Bigl( \bigl( \| \widehat A \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} + \| \widehat B \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \bigr) \bigl\| \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl( \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} + \|\psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \bigr) \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr) \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \\
                    &\qquad + T^\frac12 \bigl\| \nabla \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} (\widehat A - \widehat B)\bigr\|_{L^2_{t, x}}\bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \\
                    &\qquad + T \bigl\| \widehat A - \widehat B \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \bigl\| \nabla {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \\
                    &\qquad + T \cdot \Bigl( 1 + \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}}^2 + \| \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^\infty_x} \Bigr) \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}\\
                    &\qquad + T \cdot \Bigl( \| \nabla \,{\setlength{\fboxsep}{.5\fboxsep}\boxed{\textup{\sc g}}}\, \|_{L^\infty_x} + \| \psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \| {\bf D}_B \psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \Bigr) \bigl\| \widehat \phi - \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \\
                    &\qquad + T \cdot \Bigl( \| \widehat \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \| {\bf D}_B \psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \| \widehat \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \| \phi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} \bigl\| {\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}\Bigr) \\
                    &\lesssim_\mathsf E T \cdot \Bigl( \| \phi - \psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} + \| {\bf D}_A \phi - {\bf D}_B \psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}\Bigr) \\
                        &\qquad+ T \cdot \Bigl( \| \widehat\phi - \widehat\psi \|_{L^\infty_{t, x}} +  \| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat\psi \|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}\Bigr) ,
        \end{align*}
    using the $L^2_{t, x}$-bound from (\ref{eq:iterate-diff-A}) to control $\nabla \mathbb P^\mathrm{cf} (\widehat A - \widehat B)$, and estimating the terms in $L^\infty_{t, x}$ using an appropriate combination of Sobolev embedding (\ref{eq:GNinfty}), (\ref{eq:inefficientLinfty}) and the uniform energy bounds (\ref{eq:prev-iterate-energy}), (\ref{eq:iterate-energy}). Taking $T \ll_\mathcal E 1$, the second term in the last line can be absorbed by the left-hand sides of the previous calculations. In total, the previous three calculations yield 
        \begin{align}\label{eq:iterate-diff-phi}
            \bigl\| \widehat \phi - \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| {\bf D}_{\widehat A} \widehat \phi - {\bf D}_{\widehat B} \widehat \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x}
                \lesssim_\mathsf E T \cdot \Bigl( \bigl\| \phi - \psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} + \bigl\| {\bf D}_A  \phi - {\bf D}_{B}\psi \bigr\|_{L^\infty_t L^2_x} \Bigr). 
        \end{align}
    Combining (\ref{eq:iterate-diff-A})-(\ref{eq:iterate-diff-phi}) gives the desired inequality (\ref{eq:iterate-magn-diff}).
<!-- end proof-116 -->
